c1_dinner.talk.carmen.1.02.text: It is too sweet. Rafa is in love, so everything he cooks is sweet now.
c1_dinner.talk.carmen.1.02.speaker: carmen

c1_dinner.talk.carmen.1.04.text: With the girl from the bakery counter. He thinks I don’t know. Mothers know.
c1_dinner.talk.carmen.1.04.speaker: carmen

c1_dinner.talk.iris.1.03.text: You used to argue with your mother about the chilies all night.
c1_dinner.talk.iris.1.03.speaker: steve

c1_dinner.talk.luis.1.01.text: You still keep Dad’s chair, Luis.
c1_dinner.talk.luis.1.01.speaker: steve

c1_dinner.talk.luis.1.02.text: Frank sat there every Friday for twenty years. Nobody else fits it.
c1_dinner.talk.luis.1.02.speaker: luis

c1_dinner.talk.luis.1.03.text: When he comes home, it will be waiting for him.
c1_dinner.talk.luis.1.03.speaker: luis

c1_dinner.talk.mateo.1.02.text: Four wins, nine losses. But we lead the league in effort.
c1_dinner.talk.mateo.1.02.speaker: mateo

c1_dinner.talk.mateo.1.03.text: And my outfield can finally catch. Mostly with their faces, but it counts.
c1_dinner.talk.mateo.1.03.speaker: mateo

c1_dinner.talk.rafa.1.02.text: Forty tables, one birthday, and Mamá tasting everything twice.
c1_dinner.talk.rafa.1.02.speaker: rafa

c1_dinner.talk.rafa.1.03.text: Come to Sunday dinner for real, Steve. She sets your plate either way.
c1_dinner.talk.rafa.1.03.speaker: rafa

c1_dinner.talk.tomas.1.02.text: Eleven listeners. Twelve, if Mamá ever figures out the app.
c1_dinner.talk.tomas.1.02.speaker: tomas

c1_dinner.talk.tomas.1.03.text: Laugh now. One day the bay is going to make me famous.
c1_dinner.talk.tomas.1.03.speaker: tomas

c1_escape.order.lead.03.text: And the aquarium is across the bay. Eighteen minutes each way, even with every light green.
c1_escape.order.lead.03.speaker: steve

c1_flat.compare.find.text: The ident matches, so the recorder is fine. AutoRick and I change from day to day, like anyone would. Nora’s good morning matches perfectly. People don’t do that. Recordings do.
c1_flat.compare.find.speaker: steve

c1_flat.saturday.03.text: Coffee’s on the stove. I made it strong, the way you like it.
c1_flat.saturday.03.speaker: iris

c1_flat.saturday.05.text: Strong is fine. Whatever you like.
c1_flat.saturday.05.speaker: iris

c1_flat.sunday.04.text: I’m off to feed Admiral and the otters. Back by noon.
c1_flat.sunday.04.speaker: iris

c1_flat.sunday.05.text: On a Sunday? You used to fight for every Sunday off.
c1_flat.sunday.05.speaker: steve

c1_flat.sunday.06.text: The animals don’t know it’s Sunday, sleepyhead.
c1_flat.sunday.06.speaker: iris

c1_flat.talk.iris.1.01.text: Want some toast before you go?
c1_flat.talk.iris.1.01.speaker: steve

c1_flat.talk.iris.1.02.text: I ate already. There’s fruit in the blue bowl.
c1_flat.talk.iris.1.02.speaker: iris

c1_flat.talk.iris.1.03.text: Since when do you eat breakfast?
c1_flat.talk.iris.1.03.speaker: steve

c1_flat.talk.iris.1.04.text: For a while now. It’s good for you.
c1_flat.talk.iris.1.04.speaker: iris

c1_flat.talk.iris.2.02.text: Growing. One of them bit a volunteer again. Only a little.
c1_flat.talk.iris.2.02.speaker: iris

c1_flat.talk.iris.2.03.text: You used to say that was her best quality.
c1_flat.talk.iris.2.03.speaker: steve

c1_flat.talk.iris.2.04.text: She’s a good otter. They’re all good otters.
c1_flat.talk.iris.2.04.speaker: iris

c1_flat.talk.iris.3.02.text: He read yesterday’s weather again. Twelve years at that desk, and they replaced me with him.
c1_flat.talk.iris.3.02.speaker: steve

c1_flat.talk.iris.3.03.text: Then you have more time at home. That’s nice, isn’t it?
c1_flat.talk.iris.3.03.speaker: iris

c1_flat.talk.iris.4.03.text: You used to kick the blankets off every night. Every single night.
c1_flat.talk.iris.4.03.speaker: steve

c1_flat.talk.iris.4.04.text: Did I? I don’t remember that.
c1_flat.talk.iris.4.04.speaker: iris

c1_pier.bait.lead.03.text: June! Did you hear that hum just now?
c1_pier.bait.lead.03.speaker: steve

c1_pier.bait.lead.04.text: From the fish-shed line. It started before Agnes did.
c1_pier.bait.lead.04.speaker: calder

c1_pier.bait.lead.05.text: It was loudest down by the water, under the floating dock.
c1_pier.bait.lead.05.speaker: calder

c1_pier.bait.lead.06.text: Could you hear Agnes humming from there?
c1_pier.bait.lead.06.speaker: steve

c1_pier.bait.lead.07.text: Nobody can hear Agnes hum. She’s quieter than the fog.
c1_pier.bait.lead.07.speaker: calder

c1_pier.bait.lead.08.text: And the winch stopped halfway through. The note just kept going.
c1_pier.bait.lead.08.speaker: steve

c1_pier.talk.agnes.1.02.text: Splendid. Nobody has bought a thing since Tuesday.
c1_pier.talk.agnes.1.02.speaker: agnes

c1_pier.talk.agnes.1.04.text: It means the fish are safe, Steven. Somebody has to be on their side.
c1_pier.talk.agnes.1.04.speaker: agnes

c1_pier.talk.agnes.2.01.text: You still remember me from third grade?
c1_pier.talk.agnes.2.01.speaker: steve

c1_pier.talk.agnes.2.02.text: You took my classroom clock apart to find the tick.
c1_pier.talk.agnes.2.02.speaker: agnes

c1_pier.talk.agnes.2.04.text: With two pieces left over. It ran fast ever after.
c1_pier.talk.agnes.2.04.speaker: agnes

c1_pier.talk.calder.1.02.text: Every Sunday for twenty years. My mother bought it in this same line.
c1_pier.talk.calder.1.02.speaker: calder

c1_pier.talk.calder.1.03.text: Some things in this town don’t change. I like that about it.
c1_pier.talk.calder.1.03.speaker: calder

c1_pier.talk.calder.2.01.text: Is that Lyle by the shed? In a clean shirt?
c1_pier.talk.calder.2.01.speaker: steve

c1_pier.talk.calder.2.02.text: He asked for every Sunday off this summer. For his boys’ games.
c1_pier.talk.calder.2.02.speaker: calder

c1_pier.talk.calder.2.03.text: Since early summer he’s been my best deputy. Never late once. I keep waiting for the catch.
c1_pier.talk.calder.2.03.speaker: calder

c1_pier.talk.iris.1.02.text: Nine. He weighs more than your car.
c1_pier.talk.iris.1.02.speaker: iris

c1_pier.talk.iris.1.03.text: You bottle-fed him in our bathtub. For three weeks.
c1_pier.talk.iris.1.03.speaker: steve

c1_pier.talk.iris.1.04.text: I remember. It was a good bathtub.
c1_pier.talk.iris.1.04.speaker: iris

c1_pier.talk.iris.2.01.text: The line is long today. The crab boats came in early.
c1_pier.talk.iris.2.01.speaker: iris

c1_pier.talk.iris.2.02.text: You used to talk your way to the front of that line.
c1_pier.talk.iris.2.02.speaker: steve

c1_pier.talk.iris.2.03.text: Waiting is fine. Everyone gets a turn.
c1_pier.talk.iris.2.03.speaker: iris

c1_pier.talk.iris.3.03.text: You used to say he’d come to that whistle through a hurricane.
c1_pier.talk.iris.3.03.speaker: steve

c1_pier.talk.iris.3.04.text: Then you should visit him more often, sleepyhead.
c1_pier.talk.iris.3.04.speaker: iris

c1_pier.talk.lyle_copy.1.02.text: My oldest, then his brother. I’ll be in the stands for every inning.
c1_pier.talk.lyle_copy.1.02.speaker: lyle_copy

c1_pier.talk.lyle_copy.1.04.text: I made them a promise. I keep my promises now.
c1_pier.talk.lyle_copy.1.04.speaker: lyle_copy

c1_pier.talk.pell.1.02.text: Every route runs on schedule, Mr. Mercer.
c1_pier.talk.pell.1.02.speaker: pell

p_bay.talk.helen.1.01.text: Think the boy will come out with us next time?
p_bay.talk.helen.1.01.speaker: frank

p_bay.talk.helen.1.02.text: He’ll say he has a shift. Then he’ll call tomorrow and ask what we heard.
p_bay.talk.helen.1.02.speaker: helen

p_bay.talk.helen.1.04.text: He’s your son, Frank. He can’t leave a sound alone.
p_bay.talk.helen.1.04.speaker: helen

p_bay.talk.helen.2.02.text: Gloves are in the tackle box. Under the logbook.
p_bay.talk.helen.2.02.speaker: frank

p_bay.talk.helen.2.03.text: Of course they are. Everything in this boat is under the logbook.
p_bay.talk.helen.2.03.speaker: helen

p_bay.talk.helen.3.01.text: Listen. It goes up at the end, like a question.
p_bay.talk.helen.3.01.speaker: helen

p_bay.talk.helen.3.02.text: Then write it down. Time, place, what it does.
p_bay.talk.helen.3.02.speaker: frank

p_bay.talk.helen.3.03.text: Eleven-oh-five. Rowboat. It sounds like it’s waiting for someone.
p_bay.talk.helen.3.03.speaker: helen

c1_flat.sunday.find.text: Blue cassette, Sunday, 7:15. The ident, the radio, Nora and me, all over again. Now I can time the machine.
c1_flat.sunday.find.speaker: steve

c1_flat.talk.iris.3.01.text: I heard the new radio host this morning. He sounds cheerful.
c1_flat.talk.iris.3.01.speaker: iris

c10_live.first.lead.02.text: Careful. Two Pier lamps are still on from the rehearsal. Don’t count those.
c10_live.first.lead.02.speaker: nora

c10_live.second.lead.02.text: With the coast plugged in, Reed and Bell both answered two beats late. With the coast unplugged, Reed went quiet.
c10_live.second.lead.02.speaker: frank

c10_live.second.lead.03.text: Bell kept answering anyway. So Bell is only an echo inside the building.
c10_live.second.lead.03.speaker: frank

c10_report.echo.lead.01.text: Last winter the boats came in empty. I let every one of them pay me in spring.
c10_report.echo.lead.01.speaker: agnes

c10_report.survey.lead.02.text: Three slips. Reef Six has water and air, and a beacon there answers every call.
c10_report.survey.lead.02.speaker: archivist

c10_report.survey.lead.03.text: Sound Four has air, but no water at all. Reach Two has water and air, and it was visited three times.
c10_report.survey.lead.03.speaker: archivist

c10_station.playlist.lead.02.text: Three slips. My station ident, a traffic report and a news bulletin.
c10_station.playlist.lead.02.speaker: steve

c10_station.playlist.lead.03.text: The ident never stops the music. Traffic waits until the song ends. A bulletin puts a person on the air.
c10_station.playlist.lead.03.speaker: steve

c10_station.relay.lead.03.text: Gull here. Cedar and Marsh both say four. Marsh says the wind just turned west out at the Point.
c10_station.relay.lead.03.speaker: operator

c10_station.relay.lead.04.text: Ask them both about the wind again, Gull.
c10_station.relay.lead.04.speaker: frank

c10_station.relay.lead.05.text: Marsh says it’s dropping now. Cedar said the same words as last time, exactly.
c10_station.relay.lead.05.speaker: operator

c10_station.route.lead.02.text: Birch was your fixed tester. Ash was the old rehearsal loop. Elm followed Shaw’s hand.
c10_station.route.lead.02.speaker: steve

c10_station.route.lead.03.text: Returns: A is the booth echo, B is a shore camera, and C is measured aboard their ship.
c10_station.route.lead.03.speaker: wen

c10_station.talk.autorick.1.01.text: Good morning, Rick. How are you feeling today?
c10_station.talk.autorick.1.01.speaker: steve

c10_station.talk.autorick.1.02.text: I am excellent! It is currently yesterday!
c10_station.talk.autorick.1.02.speaker: autorick

c10_station.talk.frank.1.01.text: Has anybody got dry socks? I’ll trade a perfectly good vacuum tube.
c10_station.talk.frank.1.01.speaker: frank

c10_station.talk.frank.1.02.text: There’s a lost and found behind the coffee machine.
c10_station.talk.frank.1.02.speaker: steve

c10_station.talk.frank.1.03.text: Then I’m saving the world in somebody’s bowling socks.
c10_station.talk.frank.1.03.speaker: frank

c10_station.talk.frank.2.01.text: I wired half this booth, you know. Labeled every cable.
c10_station.talk.frank.2.01.speaker: frank

c10_station.talk.frank.2.02.text: Somebody took the labels off when the new owners came.
c10_station.talk.frank.2.02.speaker: steve

c10_station.talk.frank.2.03.text: Then I’ll put them back. Every single one. After breakfast.
c10_station.talk.frank.2.03.speaker: frank

c10_station.talk.stephen.1.01.text: Is there coffee? I remember liking coffee.
c10_station.talk.stephen.1.01.speaker: stephen

c10_station.talk.stephen.1.03.text: Good. That one is still mine. I’m keeping it.
c10_station.talk.stephen.1.03.speaker: stephen

c10_station.talk.stephen.2.01.text: Do we both talk on air, or do we take turns?
c10_station.talk.stephen.2.01.speaker: stephen

c10_station.talk.stephen.2.02.text: Take turns. People will think the radio is broken.
c10_station.talk.stephen.2.02.speaker: steve

c10_station.talk.stephen.2.03.text: People already think that. I listened to your replacement for a week.
c10_station.talk.stephen.2.03.speaker: stephen

c10_station.talk.wen.1.01.text: When I was a girl, our village had one loudspeaker on a pole.
c10_station.talk.wen.1.01.speaker: wen

c10_station.talk.wen.1.02.text: What did the loudspeaker play all day?
c10_station.talk.wen.1.02.speaker: steve

c10_station.talk.wen.1.03.text: Weather, news and my aunt’s opinions. Mostly my aunt’s opinions.
c10_station.talk.wen.1.03.speaker: wen

c10_town.lights.lead.02.text: Pier can see Orchard’s porch lights from the harbor. Orchard faces the hills, so they can’t see Pier at all.
c10_town.lights.lead.02.speaker: nora

c10_town.lights.lead.03.text: Both streets have the radio on. And Mateo wants one phone kept free for the fire crew.
c10_town.lights.lead.03.speaker: nora

c10_town.talk.agnes.1.01.text: You were a good student, Steven. Too loud. I liked that.
c10_town.talk.agnes.1.01.speaker: agnes

c10_town.talk.agnes.1.02.text: You weren’t really my teacher, were you?
c10_town.talk.agnes.1.02.speaker: steve

c10_town.talk.agnes.1.03.text: She was. I learned her very carefully. I only kept her chair warm.
c10_town.talk.agnes.1.03.speaker: agnes

c10_town.talk.agnes.2.01.text: Why a bait stall, of all things?
c10_town.talk.agnes.2.01.speaker: steve

c10_town.talk.agnes.2.02.text: Nobody buys bait, so nobody stays long. And I could watch the water all day.
c10_town.talk.agnes.2.02.speaker: agnes

c10_town.talk.carmen.1.01.text: I have called the bakery, the church and both bars. The bars were awake.
c10_town.talk.carmen.1.01.speaker: carmen

c10_town.talk.carmen.1.02.text: Thank you, Carmen. I mean it.
c10_town.talk.carmen.1.02.speaker: steve

c10_town.talk.carmen.1.03.text: Thank me by eating something. You haven’t eaten since Thursday. I can tell.
c10_town.talk.carmen.1.03.speaker: carmen

c10_town.talk.carmen.2.01.text: She argued with me twice tonight already. Twice, Steve!
c10_town.talk.carmen.2.01.speaker: carmen

c10_town.talk.carmen.2.03.text: It is the best night of my whole life.
c10_town.talk.carmen.2.03.speaker: carmen

c10_town.talk.nora.1.01.text: My mother has called forty people already. Thirty of them owe her money.
c10_town.talk.nora.1.01.speaker: nora

c10_town.talk.nora.1.02.text: Wait. People actually owe Carmen money?
c10_town.talk.nora.1.02.speaker: steve

c10_town.talk.nora.1.03.text: Tabs at the restaurant. She’s calling in every single one tonight.
c10_town.talk.nora.1.03.speaker: nora

c10_town.talk.nora.2.01.text: Yesterday I was asleep under the bay. Today I’m running a town.
c10_town.talk.nora.2.01.speaker: nora

c10_town.talk.nora.2.02.text: You were always running the town, Nor.
c10_town.talk.nora.2.02.speaker: steve

c10_town.talk.nora.2.03.text: True. But now people are actually listening to me.
c10_town.talk.nora.2.03.speaker: nora

c10_town.talk.nora.3.01.text: Iris called my brothers before I could. She knew every number by heart.
c10_town.talk.nora.3.01.speaker: nora

c10_town.talk.nora.3.02.text: She’s had your phone for five months.
c10_town.talk.nora.3.02.speaker: steve

c10_town.talk.nora.3.03.text: I want that phone back. And she rearranged all my apps.
c10_town.talk.nora.3.03.speaker: nora

c10_town.talk.shaw.1.01.text: I brought the fog machine. Just in case.
c10_town.talk.shaw.1.01.speaker: shaw

c10_town.talk.shaw.1.03.text: In case it needs to look impressive. It always needs to look impressive.
c10_town.talk.shaw.1.03.speaker: shaw

c10_town.talk.ward.1.01.text: My staff wanted a long speech. I told them to listen to local radio.
c10_town.talk.ward.1.01.speaker: ward

c10_town.talk.ward.1.02.text: How is your wrist, Madam President?
c10_town.talk.ward.1.02.speaker: steve

c10_town.talk.ward.1.03.text: Bandaged, and still mine. Thank you for that.
c10_town.talk.ward.1.03.speaker: ward

c10_town.talk.wen.1.01.text: Nine years ago I would have unplugged her lamps.
c10_town.talk.wen.1.01.speaker: wen

c10_town.talk.wen.1.02.text: You tried. And my fake fooled more generals than yours.
c10_town.talk.wen.1.02.speaker: shaw

c10_town.wind.lead.02.text: The fleet should hear home first. Then a voice answering them, live, that nobody recorded.
c10_town.wind.lead.02.speaker: steve

c1_dinner.talk.tomas.2.01.text: Come on my show sometime, Steve. A real sound engineer would double my ratings.
c1_dinner.talk.tomas.2.01.speaker: tomas

c1_dinner.talk.tomas.2.03.text: Nora used to call in every week just to correct my tide tables. I miss that, honestly.
c1_dinner.talk.tomas.2.03.speaker: tomas

c1_pier.talk.iris.3.01.text: You still whistle for him every Sunday?
c1_pier.talk.iris.3.01.speaker: steve

c1_pier.talk.iris.3.02.text: Every Sunday. Two notes. He always comes.
c1_pier.talk.iris.3.02.speaker: iris

c2_aquarium.guard.lead.02.text: A real person never steps or coughs the same way twice. A recording does it every time.
c2_aquarium.guard.lead.02.speaker: steve

c2_aquarium.guard.lead.03.text: Six seconds at each door. Then I compare the two.
c2_aquarium.guard.lead.03.speaker: steve

c2_aquarium.intercom.lead.03.text: Her second note goes up. Like it always did, before this summer.
c2_aquarium.intercom.lead.03.speaker: steve

c2_aquarium.intercom.lead.04.text: And there’s a loose copy of the whistle in the drawer. On that one, the second note falls.
c2_aquarium.intercom.lead.04.speaker: steve

c2_aquarium.plan.lead.01.text: On the old plan, the café and the public tank lead to the visitor hall. Door one leads to the north wing.
c2_aquarium.plan.lead.01.speaker: steve

c2_aquarium.plan.lead.02.text: But this newer notice says door one is bricked up. The service door still opens into the pump room.
c2_aquarium.plan.lead.02.speaker: steve

c2_aquarium.plan.lead.03.text: And the notice says to follow the one pipe that carries water away from the pump.
c2_aquarium.plan.lead.03.speaker: steve

c2_ship.command.lead.04.text: The chair’s little lamp stayed dark when the attendant asked. It lit up for the voice on the intercom.
c2_ship.command.lead.04.speaker: steve

c2_ship.command.lead.05.text: Dad’s counter ticks once a second. The lamp lit at tick three. The buckle clicked at tick seven.
c2_ship.command.lead.05.speaker: steve

c2_ship.escape.lead.02.text: Dad’s recorder caught three voices tonight. Nora’s spool, the attendant, and the Prefect.
c2_ship.escape.lead.02.speaker: steve

c2_ship.escape.lead.04.text: When my sleeve brushed the other grille, the chair’s lamp blinked.
c2_ship.escape.lead.04.speaker: steve

c2_ship.escape.lead.05.text: The lamp stays lit for one second each beat. At the notch marked sixty-one, it stays lit for six.
c2_ship.escape.lead.05.speaker: steve

c2_ship.nora.lead.03.text: The corridor light flashes at two, six and ten seconds. Every four seconds, like a clock.
c2_ship.nora.lead.03.speaker: steve

c2_ship.nora.lead.04.text: The pickup on the rail repeats each flash, one second late.
c2_ship.nora.lead.04.speaker: steve

c2_ship.nora.lead.05.text: And there’s fog on the glass above her mouth. Three seconds, seven, then twelve.
c2_ship.nora.lead.05.speaker: steve

c2_ship.nora.lead.06.text: I made a rubbing of each rhythm. Now the labels have come off.
c2_ship.nora.lead.06.speaker: steve

c2_ship.talk.iris.1.01.text: Where are we, Nor? What is this place?
c2_ship.talk.iris.1.01.speaker: steve

c2_ship.talk.iris.1.02.text: Somewhere safe, under the bay. Please don’t be frightened.
c2_ship.talk.iris.1.02.speaker: iris

c2_ship.talk.iris.1.03.text: You walked me down that tunnel yourself.
c2_ship.talk.iris.1.03.speaker: steve

c2_ship.talk.iris.1.04.text: They asked me to. I always do what I am asked.
c2_ship.talk.iris.1.04.speaker: iris

c2_ship.talk.iris.2.01.text: Do you remember the day we met?
c2_ship.talk.iris.2.01.speaker: steve

c2_ship.talk.iris.2.02.text: At the aquarium. You fixed the underwater speakers. You had a coffee stain on your green shirt.
c2_ship.talk.iris.2.02.speaker: iris

c2_ship.talk.iris.2.04.text: I remember everything she saw. Everything I saw.
c2_ship.talk.iris.2.04.speaker: iris

c2_ship.talk.iris.3.01.text: Carmen keeps my plate warm every Sunday. Does she know her daughter is down here?
c2_ship.talk.iris.3.01.speaker: steve

c2_ship.talk.iris.3.02.text: Carmen is happy. Everyone at that table is happy.
c2_ship.talk.iris.3.02.speaker: iris

c2_ship.talk.iris.3.04.text: It is the only one I am allowed to give you.
c2_ship.talk.iris.3.04.speaker: iris

c2_ship.talk.lyle_copy.1.01.text: Lyle, do your boys know where you are tonight?
c2_ship.talk.lyle_copy.1.01.speaker: steve

c2_ship.talk.lyle_copy.1.02.text: They’re asleep. I’ll be at their game on Sunday. I always am now.
c2_ship.talk.lyle_copy.1.02.speaker: lyle_copy

c2_ship.talk.lyle_copy.1.03.text: You used to miss every single one.
c2_ship.talk.lyle_copy.1.03.speaker: steve

c2_ship.talk.lyle_copy.1.04.text: People change, Steve. Mostly for the better.
c2_ship.talk.lyle_copy.1.04.speaker: lyle_copy

c2_ship.talk.lyle_copy.2.01.text: You’re a deputy, Lyle. You swore an oath to this town.
c2_ship.talk.lyle_copy.2.01.speaker: steve

c2_ship.talk.lyle_copy.2.02.text: I did. I remember every word of it.
c2_ship.talk.lyle_copy.2.02.speaker: lyle_copy

c2_ship.talk.lyle_copy.2.03.text: Then get me out of this chair.
c2_ship.talk.lyle_copy.2.03.speaker: steve

c2_ship.talk.lyle_copy.2.04.text: I am helping you, Steve. This is the easy way.
c2_ship.talk.lyle_copy.2.04.speaker: lyle_copy

c3_archive.cycle.lead.03.text: Each box has two dates. The night I recorded, and the day the episode aired.
c3_archive.cycle.lead.03.speaker: tomas

c3_archive.cycle.lead.04.text: The pier lamp always dims first, at 23:42. Footsteps pass the boathouse at 23:53.
c3_archive.cycle.lead.04.speaker: tomas

c3_archive.cycle.lead.05.text: And at four minutes past midnight, the water starts to glow.
c3_archive.cycle.lead.05.speaker: tomas

c3_archive.cycle.lead.06.text: I want to see faces on that path before they reach the water. Without anyone seeing us.
c3_archive.cycle.lead.06.speaker: calder

c3_archive.cycle.lead.07.text: From the sea wall, the path is behind you. The pier is wide open. The boathouse window faces the path.
c3_archive.cycle.lead.07.speaker: tomas

c3_archive.paper.lead.03.text: The ledger was signed in ink, right here at the counter. May third, ten past two, with the clerk’s stamp.
c3_archive.paper.lead.03.speaker: calder

c3_archive.paper.lead.04.text: The computer entry was typed in from the ledger the next day. Somebody has changed it since.
c3_archive.paper.lead.04.speaker: calder

c3_archive.paper.lead.05.text: This hearing transcript has Walt in Washington that afternoon, answering questions from half past one until four.
c3_archive.paper.lead.05.speaker: steve

c3_archive.paper.lead.06.text: And the newspaper column only says he looked tired.
c3_archive.paper.lead.06.speaker: steve

c3_archive.paper.lead.07.text: The permit reopens the aquarium’s old seawater intake. The same tunnel they walked you down.
c3_archive.paper.lead.07.speaker: calder

c3_archive.power.lead.07.text: Here are last month’s meter rolls. Sentinel Point, and Pearl Laundry next door.
c3_archive.power.lead.07.speaker: calder

c3_archive.power.lead.08.text: They’re running totals, like the miles on a car. What counts is how far each one moved.
c3_archive.power.lead.08.speaker: steve

c3_archive.talk.agnes.1.01.text: You came all the way here on the bus?
c3_archive.talk.agnes.1.01.speaker: steve

c3_archive.talk.agnes.1.02.text: The number four. The driver and I have an arrangement.
c3_archive.talk.agnes.1.02.speaker: agnes

c3_archive.talk.agnes.1.03.text: What kind of arrangement is that?
c3_archive.talk.agnes.1.03.speaker: steve

c3_archive.talk.agnes.1.04.text: He drives, and I correct his grammar. We both arrive improved.
c3_archive.talk.agnes.1.04.speaker: agnes

c3_archive.talk.agnes.2.01.text: I like archives, Steven. Somebody should keep what everyone else forgets.
c3_archive.talk.agnes.2.01.speaker: agnes

c3_archive.talk.agnes.2.02.text: Is that why you came all this way?
c3_archive.talk.agnes.2.02.speaker: steve

c3_archive.talk.agnes.2.03.text: I came to sell you a herring. Two dollars, please. Exact change.
c3_archive.talk.agnes.2.03.speaker: agnes

c3_archive.talk.calder.1.01.text: Why does the sheriff have keys to the archive?
c3_archive.talk.calder.1.01.speaker: steve

c3_archive.talk.calder.1.02.text: The sheriff’s office has had a key since nineteen fifty. Nobody ever asked for it back.
c3_archive.talk.calder.1.02.speaker: calder

c3_archive.talk.calder.1.03.text: Ruth used to say I’d rather read old permits than novels. She was right.
c3_archive.talk.calder.1.03.speaker: calder

c3_archive.talk.calder.2.01.text: The President is coming here? To Bellwether?
c3_archive.talk.calder.2.01.speaker: steve

c3_archive.talk.calder.2.02.text: November seventh. The Rotary Club is already fighting about the bunting.
c3_archive.talk.calder.2.02.speaker: calder

c3_archive.talk.calder.2.03.text: I’ve been asked to close Harbor Road and smile. I can manage one of those.
c3_archive.talk.calder.2.03.speaker: calder

c3_archive.talk.tomas.1.01.text: How many listeners does the podcast have now?
c3_archive.talk.tomas.1.01.speaker: steve

c3_archive.talk.tomas.1.02.text: Fourteen. Mamá found the app, and now she leaves comments.
c3_archive.talk.tomas.1.02.speaker: tomas

c3_archive.talk.tomas.1.03.text: Every episode, the same comment. Eat something, mijo.
c3_archive.talk.tomas.1.03.speaker: tomas

c3_archive.talk.tomas.1.04.text: She’s not wrong, you know, Tomás.
c3_archive.talk.tomas.1.04.speaker: steve

c3_archive.talk.tomas.2.02.text: Last night. No capitals, no apostrophes, same as always.
c3_archive.talk.tomas.2.02.speaker: tomas

c3_archive.talk.tomas.2.03.text: She just wrote, eat something. She sounds like Mamá now. That’s new.
c3_archive.talk.tomas.2.03.speaker: tomas

c3_archive.talk.tomas.3.01.text: Do you know how many boxes are down here?
c3_archive.talk.tomas.3.01.speaker: tomas

c3_archive.talk.tomas.3.02.text: No, but I bet you counted them.
c3_archive.talk.tomas.3.02.speaker: steve

c3_archive.talk.tomas.3.03.text: Four hundred and twelve. I counted while June looked for the light switch.
c3_archive.talk.tomas.3.03.speaker: tomas

c3_archive.talk.tomas.3.04.text: You’d get along with Mrs. Penhallow.
c3_archive.talk.tomas.3.04.speaker: steve

c3_house.crossword.lead.04.text: I called 911 on Sunday night, when people walked into the water. That was before the chair.
c3_house.crossword.lead.04.speaker: steve

c3_house.crossword.lead.05.text: After midnight, the 911 line rings in my kitchen. My machine keeps every call. I haven’t played Sunday’s yet.
c3_house.crossword.lead.05.speaker: calder

c3_house.mail.lead.04.text: Dale’s bag left the post office at four minutes past eight, with your letters already bundled for my house.
c3_house.mail.lead.04.speaker: calder

c3_house.mail.lead.05.text: I didn’t phone the post office until twelve past eight. And Carmen only heard from Nora at lunch.
c3_house.mail.lead.05.speaker: calder

c3_house.rules.lead.02.text: Gus Albano. Thirty years of his grandmother’s recipes, and on Monday a new pastry in his window.
c3_house.rules.lead.02.speaker: calder

c3_house.talk.calder.1.01.text: Does Biscuit ever wake up, June?
c3_house.talk.calder.1.01.speaker: steve

c3_house.talk.calder.1.02.text: For cheese. And once for a thunderstorm, back in two thousand nineteen.
c3_house.talk.calder.1.02.speaker: calder

c3_house.talk.calder.1.03.text: Some guard dog you have there.
c3_house.talk.calder.1.03.speaker: steve

c3_house.talk.calder.1.04.text: Ruth picked her out. She said a sheriff needs one partner who never argues.
c3_house.talk.calder.1.04.speaker: calder

c3_house.talk.calder.2.01.text: You really do the crossword in ink, every single morning?
c3_house.talk.calder.2.01.speaker: steve

c3_house.talk.calder.2.02.text: Ruth started it. She said pencils are for people who expect to be wrong.
c3_house.talk.calder.2.02.speaker: calder

c3_house.talk.calder.2.04.text: Every day, Mercer. I just commit to it.
c3_house.talk.calder.2.04.speaker: calder

c3_house.talk.calder.3.01.text: What are we going to do with forty-eight casseroles?
c3_house.talk.calder.3.01.speaker: steve

c3_house.talk.calder.3.02.text: Eat Carmen’s tonight. The deputies get the rest, except the tuna one.
c3_house.talk.calder.3.02.speaker: calder

c3_house.talk.calder.3.03.text: What’s wrong with the tuna one?
c3_house.talk.calder.3.03.speaker: steve

c3_house.talk.calder.3.04.text: Potato chips on top. I have standards, even in a crisis.
c3_house.talk.calder.3.04.speaker: calder

c3_house.talk.calder.4.01.text: How long have you kept that list, June?
c3_house.talk.calder.4.01.speaker: steve

c3_house.talk.calder.4.02.text: Since last fall. The town got nicer, and nobody could tell me why.
c3_house.talk.calder.4.02.speaker: calder

c3_house.talk.calder.4.03.text: In my job, when everybody suddenly behaves, you start counting.
c3_house.talk.calder.4.03.speaker: calder

c3_house.talk.carmen.1.01.text: How is Nora doing, Carmen? Really?
c3_house.talk.carmen.1.01.speaker: steve

c3_house.talk.carmen.1.02.text: Calm. So calm. She agrees with me about everything now.
c3_house.talk.carmen.1.02.speaker: carmen

c3_house.talk.carmen.1.03.text: I should be happy, mijo. But I miss the fights. Is that terrible?
c3_house.talk.carmen.1.03.speaker: carmen

c3_house.talk.carmen.1.04.text: No, it isn’t. I miss them too.
c3_house.talk.carmen.1.04.speaker: steve

c3_house.talk.carmen.2.01.text: The man at the market, Carmen. What did he say to you?
c3_house.talk.carmen.2.01.speaker: steve

c3_house.talk.carmen.2.02.text: That the tomatoes looked lovely. You never say lovely, Steve. Not once in four years.
c3_house.talk.carmen.2.02.speaker: carmen

c3_house.talk.carmen.2.03.text: I thought you were finally getting better.
c3_house.talk.carmen.2.03.speaker: carmen

c3_house.talk.carmen.3.01.text: What did you bring us, Carmen?
c3_house.talk.carmen.3.01.speaker: steve

c3_house.talk.carmen.3.02.text: Chicken tinga. Rafa made it, so it is too sweet. He is still in love.
c3_house.talk.carmen.3.02.speaker: carmen

c3_house.talk.carmen.3.03.text: With the girl from the bakery counter?
c3_house.talk.carmen.3.03.speaker: steve

c3_house.talk.carmen.3.04.text: Now he brings home day-old bread every night. We are drowning in bread.
c3_house.talk.carmen.3.04.speaker: carmen

c3_house.talk.pell.1.01.text: Cold out there this morning, Dale?
c3_house.talk.pell.1.01.speaker: steve

c3_house.talk.pell.1.02.text: Eleven degrees at eight o’clock. Wind from the west at nine knots.
c3_house.talk.pell.1.02.speaker: pell

c3_house.talk.pell.1.03.text: I only meant, is it cold.
c3_house.talk.pell.1.03.speaker: steve

c3_house.talk.pell.1.04.text: It is within the normal range for October.
c3_house.talk.pell.1.04.speaker: pell

c3_house.talk.pell.2.01.text: You still bring letters for my parents, Dale.
c3_house.talk.pell.2.01.speaker: steve

c3_house.talk.pell.2.02.text: Every item goes to its address. That is the procedure.
c3_house.talk.pell.2.02.speaker: pell

c3_house.talk.pell.2.03.text: They’ve been gone for eighteen months.
c3_house.talk.pell.2.03.speaker: steve

c3_house.talk.pell.2.04.text: The address has not changed, Mr. Mercer.
c3_house.talk.pell.2.04.speaker: pell

c4_escape.fault.lead.02.text: Yesterday’s log says what each card does. SILVER moves the signer. BLUE moves his whole corridor. WHITE moves everyone else.
c4_escape.fault.lead.02.speaker: steve

c4_escape.fault.lead.03.text: The van escort signed tonight’s ticket, and he works my corridor. Four of us sleep on the west side.
c4_escape.fault.lead.03.speaker: steve

c4_escape.tube.lead.03.text: The night list says June moved out of OAK, into the room across from the linen cupboard.
c4_escape.tube.lead.03.speaker: steve

c4_escape.tube.lead.04.text: Standard capsules stop at Rook’s desk for sorting. The blue maintenance ones go straight through.
c4_escape.tube.lead.04.speaker: steve

c4_escape.van.lead.02.text: The driver radios before he slows. First a brick bridge over the canal, then a gravel bend.
c4_escape.van.lead.02.speaker: steve

c4_escape.van.lead.03.text: After the gravel comes the weighbridge. There, the escort opens the door himself.
c4_escape.van.lead.03.speaker: steve

c4_safe.ctx.04.text: On the drive, every station talked about President Ward. On November seventh she signs an accord with China at Sentinel Point.
c4_safe.ctx.04.speaker: steve

c4_safe.match.lead.03.text: Remember Nora’s good morning? Two days, same breath, same pause. People never do that. Recordings do.
c4_safe.match.lead.03.speaker: steve

c4_safe.record.lead.03.text: If you record Adrian, Mercer, I want to hear this house around his voice. Not my phone.
c4_safe.record.lead.03.speaker: calder

c4_safe.record.lead.04.text: The lounge has the karaoke machine, and the generator roars right under June’s window.
c4_safe.record.lead.04.speaker: steve

c4_safe.record.lead.05.text: But his office door has a gap at the bottom. And he speaks a second after the music stops.
c4_safe.record.lead.05.speaker: steve

c4_safe.screens.lead.05.text: In the aquarium, a picture that kept repeating meant nobody was really there.
c4_safe.screens.lead.05.speaker: steve

c4_safe.talk.calder.1.01.text: Who is looking after Biscuit while you’re up here?
c4_safe.talk.calder.1.01.speaker: steve

c4_safe.talk.calder.1.02.text: Dale. He comes by twice a day with the mail anyway.
c4_safe.talk.calder.1.02.speaker: calder

c4_safe.talk.calder.1.03.text: She likes him better than me. He never forgets the treats.
c4_safe.talk.calder.1.03.speaker: calder

c4_safe.talk.calder.2.01.text: My father brought me up here to fish when I was a girl. We never caught a thing.
c4_safe.talk.calder.2.01.speaker: calder

c4_safe.talk.calder.2.02.text: Then why did you keep coming?
c4_safe.talk.calder.2.02.speaker: steve

c4_safe.talk.calder.2.03.text: For the sandwiches. And three whole hours where nobody could phone him.
c4_safe.talk.calder.2.03.speaker: calder

c4_safe.talk.calder.3.01.text: Adrian and I worked a case together twenty years ago. He argued with everyone, including me.
c4_safe.talk.calder.3.01.speaker: calder

c4_safe.talk.calder.3.02.text: He hasn’t argued with anybody since he got here.
c4_safe.talk.calder.3.02.speaker: steve

c4_safe.talk.calder.3.03.text: No. He hasn’t. I noticed that too.
c4_safe.talk.calder.3.03.speaker: calder

c4_safe.talk.rook_copy.1.01.text: Nice place. Does the Bureau own it?
c4_safe.talk.rook_copy.1.01.speaker: steve

c4_safe.talk.rook_copy.1.02.text: It does. Every room is exactly as the file describes. I checked them all twice.
c4_safe.talk.rook_copy.1.02.speaker: rook_copy

c4_safe.talk.rook_copy.1.03.text: You read the file on the furniture?
c4_safe.talk.rook_copy.1.03.speaker: steve

c4_safe.talk.rook_copy.1.04.text: I read everything, Steve. It saves time later.
c4_safe.talk.rook_copy.1.04.speaker: rook_copy

c4_safe.talk.rook_copy.2.01.text: June says you take your coffee with three sugars.
c4_safe.talk.rook_copy.2.01.speaker: steve

c4_safe.talk.rook_copy.2.02.text: I take it however the house makes it.
c4_safe.talk.rook_copy.2.02.speaker: rook_copy

c4_safe.talk.rook_copy.2.04.text: It’s a very good answer. It never disappoints anyone.
c4_safe.talk.rook_copy.2.04.speaker: rook_copy

c5_shack.log.lead.03.text: Your father asked me what the bay sounded like. I told him, like a whole church humming one hymn.
c5_shack.log.lead.03.speaker: luis

c5_shack.rig.lead.04.text: His log says the dial reads a little high. The same amount, every time.
c5_shack.rig.lead.04.speaker: steve

c5_shack.talk.luis.1.01.text: How is Carmen holding up, Luis?
c5_shack.talk.luis.1.01.speaker: steve

c5_shack.talk.luis.1.02.text: She cooks. When she is frightened, she cooks for forty people. The freezer is full of tamales.
c5_shack.talk.luis.1.02.speaker: luis

c5_shack.talk.luis.1.03.text: Take some with you when you go. She would want you fed, even now.
c5_shack.talk.luis.1.03.speaker: luis

c5_shack.talk.luis.2.01.text: Did Dad ever bring you up here?
c5_shack.talk.luis.2.01.speaker: steve

c5_shack.talk.luis.2.02.text: Every spring. He tuned that radio for hours, and I fell asleep in that chair.
c5_shack.talk.luis.2.02.speaker: luis

c5_shack.talk.luis.2.03.text: He said I snored in perfect pitch. It was the nicest thing he ever said to me.
c5_shack.talk.luis.2.03.speaker: luis

c5_shack.talk.luis.3.01.text: Luis, did Nora seem different to you lately?
c5_shack.talk.luis.3.01.speaker: steve

c5_shack.talk.luis.3.02.text: Last month she let her mother win an argument about salt. Nora never lets anybody win anything.
c5_shack.talk.luis.3.02.speaker: luis

c5_shack.talk.luis.3.03.text: I thought she was finally growing up. Now I don’t know what I thought.
c5_shack.talk.luis.3.03.speaker: luis

c5_shack.talk.operator.1.01.text: What did Dad talk about on Thursday nights?
c5_shack.talk.operator.1.01.speaker: steve

c5_shack.talk.operator.1.02.text: Antennas, mostly. And your mother’s soup. He described every spoonful over the air.
c5_shack.talk.operator.1.02.speaker: operator

c5_shack.talk.operator.1.03.text: Cedar always said Frank’s soup reports were the best show on the band.
c5_shack.talk.operator.1.03.speaker: operator

c5_shack.talk.operator.2.01.text: Marsh has the tallest antenna in the county, out past Sentinel Point. Says the fog up there hums at night.
c5_shack.talk.operator.2.01.speaker: operator

c5_shack.talk.operator.2.02.text: Tell Marsh I’d like to hear that sometime.
c5_shack.talk.operator.2.02.speaker: steve

c5_shack.talk.operator.2.03.text: Marsh will talk your ear off, kid. Bring a thermos.
c5_shack.talk.operator.2.03.speaker: operator

c5_station.automation.lead.02.text: The maintenance door only unlatches while my ident plays. Twelve seconds. But the walk over there takes fifteen.
c5_station.automation.lead.02.speaker: steve

c5_station.automation.lead.03.text: And the news cart is locked. It only plays on the hour, and it’s twenty past.
c5_station.automation.lead.03.speaker: steve

c5_station.halcyon.lead.02.text: Three early nights in September. Halcyon said they were saving on my overtime.
c5_station.halcyon.lead.02.speaker: steve

c5_station.halcyon.lead.03.text: And the tower log says the tower ran by itself on those same three nights.
c5_station.halcyon.lead.03.speaker: steve

c5_station.sleeve.lead.02.text: Mom never wrote my first show. She wrote my first night at the desk. The engineer sits at the desk.
c5_station.sleeve.lead.02.speaker: steve

c5_station.stephen.lead.04.text: A tape that says Mom, last call? Mom never leaves voicemails. She calls back.
c5_station.stephen.lead.04.speaker: stephen

c5_station.stephen.lead.05.text: Then turn this poster over, and read it.
c5_station.stephen.lead.05.speaker: steve

c5_station.talk.autorick.1.01.text: All right, machine. What’s the weather tonight?
c5_station.talk.autorick.1.01.speaker: steve

c5_station.talk.autorick.1.02.text: Sunny and seventy-two, folks! Perfect beach weather out there in Bellwether!
c5_station.talk.autorick.1.02.speaker: autorick

c5_station.talk.autorick.1.03.text: It’s midnight in November. That was yesterday’s weather, and it was wrong then too.
c5_station.talk.autorick.1.03.speaker: steve

c5_station.talk.autorick.2.01.text: Can I make a request? Anything with a saxophone.
c5_station.talk.autorick.2.01.speaker: steve

c5_station.talk.autorick.2.02.text: Our request line is closed! Every song is chosen with love by Halcyon Media Holdings.
c5_station.talk.autorick.2.02.speaker: autorick

c5_station.talk.autorick.2.03.text: Chosen with love. By a spreadsheet in another state.
c5_station.talk.autorick.2.03.speaker: steve

c5_station.talk.autorick.3.01.text: Good night, Bellwether! Keep one ear on the water!
c5_station.talk.autorick.3.01.speaker: autorick

c5_station.talk.autorick.3.02.text: I wrote that sign-off. My first week on the night desk.
c5_station.talk.autorick.3.02.speaker: steve

c5_station.talk.autorick.3.03.text: Dad called the station the next morning just to say he heard it.
c5_station.talk.autorick.3.03.speaker: steve

c6_iris.alibi.lead.02.text: Gus sets his oven clock four minutes fast. He says it keeps the bread honest.
c6_iris.alibi.lead.02.speaker: stephen

c6_iris.alibi.lead.03.text: The bus clock runs two minutes slow. The florist sets hers by the radio, like a sensible person.
c6_iris.alibi.lead.03.speaker: stephen

c6_iris.alibi.lead.04.text: And Gus has my poster in his window. He asks everyone to help him fix the smudge.
c6_iris.alibi.lead.04.speaker: stephen

c6_iris.talk.autorick.1.01.text: Police are still looking for Steve Mercer. If you see him, tell him to smile!
c6_iris.talk.autorick.1.01.speaker: autorick

c6_iris.talk.autorick.1.02.text: He never smiles before ten. I can vouch for that personally.
c6_iris.talk.autorick.1.02.speaker: stephen

c6_iris.talk.iris.1.01.text: Have you seen Admiral since you went missing?
c6_iris.talk.iris.1.01.speaker: steve

c6_iris.talk.iris.1.02.text: Once, at dawn on Saturday, when the pier was empty. He still won’t come to my whistle.
c6_iris.talk.iris.1.02.speaker: iris

c6_iris.talk.iris.1.03.text: He stole my sandwich anyway. I think that means we’re friends now.
c6_iris.talk.iris.1.03.speaker: iris

c6_iris.talk.iris.2.01.text: Do you even like breakfast? You always said you’d eaten already.
c6_iris.talk.iris.2.01.speaker: steve

c6_iris.talk.iris.2.02.text: I don’t like it. Nora doesn’t either. It was on a list of healthy things.
c6_iris.talk.iris.2.02.speaker: iris

c6_iris.talk.iris.2.03.text: This morning I skipped it. It felt like breaking a very small law.
c6_iris.talk.iris.2.03.speaker: iris

c6_iris.talk.iris.3.01.text: I miss Sunday dinners. Carmen shouting at the stove. Tomás explaining the moon landing to the soup.
c6_iris.talk.iris.3.01.speaker: iris

c6_iris.talk.iris.3.02.text: They miss you too. They think you’re Nora.
c6_iris.talk.iris.3.02.speaker: steve

c6_iris.talk.iris.3.03.text: I know. That is the part I can’t fix.
c6_iris.talk.iris.3.03.speaker: iris

c6_iris.talk.stephen.1.01.text: Do you still think I need a haircut?
c6_iris.talk.stephen.1.01.speaker: steve

c6_iris.talk.stephen.1.02.text: We both need one. I just look better needing it.
c6_iris.talk.stephen.1.02.speaker: stephen

c6_iris.talk.stephen.2.01.text: I slept in Dad’s chair last night. It still smells of solder and peppermints.
c6_iris.talk.stephen.2.01.speaker: stephen

c6_iris.talk.stephen.2.02.text: He kept the peppermints in the drawer with the fuses.
c6_iris.talk.stephen.2.02.speaker: steve

c6_iris.talk.stephen.2.03.text: Third drawer down. I know. I remember that part.
c6_iris.talk.stephen.2.03.speaker: stephen

c6_iris.talk.stephen.3.01.text: Everyone at the market is going to stare at me today.
c6_iris.talk.stephen.3.01.speaker: stephen

c6_iris.talk.stephen.3.03.text: I’ve never been the interesting one before. I could get used to it.
c6_iris.talk.stephen.3.03.speaker: stephen

c6_jail.mail.lead.04.text: I file by destination. The carbon says Jail, returned key. That is register entry eighteen.
c6_jail.mail.lead.04.speaker: pell

c6_jail.mail.lead.05.text: Each slot holds two entries. Slot one holds entries one and two, and so on.
c6_jail.mail.lead.05.speaker: pell

c6_jail.talk.pell.1.02.text: She eats at seven and at five. She prefers the blue bowl. I am not yet sure she prefers me.
c6_jail.talk.pell.1.02.speaker: pell

c6_jail.talk.pell.1.03.text: I am working on it. I have learned to scratch behind her left ear.
c6_jail.talk.pell.1.03.speaker: pell

c6_jail.talk.pell.2.01.text: Do you like the mail route?
c6_jail.talk.pell.2.01.speaker: steve

c6_jail.talk.pell.2.02.text: Dale’s route has two hundred and twelve stops. Dale liked eleven of them.
c6_jail.talk.pell.2.02.speaker: pell

c6_jail.talk.pell.3.01.text: What is Dale like? The real one.
c6_jail.talk.pell.3.01.speaker: steve

c6_jail.talk.pell.3.02.text: He complains about the rain, the dogs and the government. In that order.
c6_jail.talk.pell.3.02.speaker: pell

c6_jail.talk.pell.3.03.text: I have his memories, but not his complaints. I find I do not miss them.
c6_jail.talk.pell.3.03.speaker: pell

c7_gate.badge.lead.03.text: The gate card has three windows. Red at 11:10 is for deliveries on foot. No vehicles at all.
c7_gate.badge.lead.03.speaker: stephen

c7_gate.badge.lead.04.text: Gold at 11:50 is for the signers. The President’s guards search every vehicle with dogs.
c7_gate.badge.lead.04.speaker: stephen

c7_gate.badge.lead.05.text: Blue at 11:30 is for crew trucks. The guard scans the driver’s pass. If it shows green, the truck rolls through.
c7_gate.badge.lead.05.speaker: stephen

c7_gate.badge.lead.06.text: And I have no pass at all. So the guard can’t be allowed to see me.
c7_gate.badge.lead.06.speaker: steve

c7_gate.post.lead.01.text: Registered mail goes into the addressee’s own hand. Nobody else may sign for her.
c7_gate.post.lead.01.speaker: pell

c7_gate.post.lead.02.text: The press desk only stamps handouts for reporters. The stage door only signs for scenery.
c7_gate.post.lead.02.speaker: pell

c7_gate.post.lead.03.text: The delegation clerk can call the President to her hatch in person.
c7_gate.post.lead.03.speaker: pell

c7_gate.post.lead.04.text: She signs the white sheet, and her pen presses through to the yellow carbon underneath. The white sheet stays with her.
c7_gate.post.lead.04.speaker: pell

c7_gate.talk.pell.1.02.text: The Sheriff’s neighbor. I left written instructions. Four pages, with diagrams.
c7_gate.talk.pell.1.02.speaker: pell

c7_gate.talk.pell.1.04.text: She is a very important beagle. She has a schedule.
c7_gate.talk.pell.1.04.speaker: pell

c7_gate.talk.pell.2.01.text: Dale’s route has two hundred and twelve mailboxes. I know every one of them.
c7_gate.talk.pell.2.01.speaker: pell

c7_gate.talk.pell.2.02.text: Do you actually like the work?
c7_gate.talk.pell.2.02.speaker: steve

c7_gate.talk.pell.2.03.text: I like the dogs, and the people who say thank you. Mostly the dogs.
c7_gate.talk.pell.2.03.speaker: pell

c7_gate.talk.rook_copy.1.01.text: The coffee in the press tent is terrible. I’ve had four cups.
c7_gate.talk.rook_copy.1.01.speaker: rook_copy

c7_gate.talk.rook_copy.1.02.text: You don’t seem to mind it very much.
c7_gate.talk.rook_copy.1.02.speaker: stephen

c7_gate.talk.rook_copy.1.03.text: Rook takes his coffee black. I keep putting sugar in mine. I don’t know why.
c7_gate.talk.rook_copy.1.03.speaker: rook_copy

c7_gate.talk.rook_copy.2.01.text: Do you ever think about him? The one you were made from?
c7_gate.talk.rook_copy.2.01.speaker: rook_copy

c7_gate.talk.rook_copy.2.02.text: Every single day. He snores, apparently.
c7_gate.talk.rook_copy.2.02.speaker: stephen

c7_gate.talk.rook_copy.2.03.text: I wonder if mine dreams. Down there, in the cold.
c7_gate.talk.rook_copy.2.03.speaker: rook_copy

c7_gate.talk.shaw.1.01.text: This truck is older than you are. I rewired half of it myself.
c7_gate.talk.shaw.1.01.speaker: shaw

c7_gate.talk.shaw.1.03.text: Of course it does. I have good ears too. Mine are just older.
c7_gate.talk.shaw.1.03.speaker: shaw

c7_gate.talk.shaw.2.01.text: Before this, I built explosions for the movies. Six films, and never one real fire.
c7_gate.talk.shaw.2.01.speaker: shaw

c7_gate.talk.shaw.2.02.text: And now you run sound checks in the fog?
c7_gate.talk.shaw.2.02.speaker: steve

c7_gate.talk.shaw.2.03.text: The government pays worse. But the sandwiches are better.
c7_gate.talk.shaw.2.03.speaker: shaw

c7_gate.talk.stephen.1.01.text: Can you see the trucks from here? I can barely see my own feet.
c7_gate.talk.stephen.1.01.speaker: steve

c7_gate.talk.stephen.1.02.text: Good. Fog is very flattering. Nobody looks like a wanted poster in fog.
c7_gate.talk.stephen.1.02.speaker: stephen

c7_gate.talk.stephen.1.03.text: Dad used to say fog makes every sound feel closer.
c7_gate.talk.stephen.1.03.speaker: steve

c7_gate.talk.stephen.1.04.text: He said it on the boat, every summer. I remember that one. I think I do.
c7_gate.talk.stephen.1.04.speaker: stephen

c7_gate.talk.stephen.2.01.text: I had two croissants from Gus this morning. He gave me a third one for free.
c7_gate.talk.stephen.2.01.speaker: stephen

c7_gate.talk.stephen.2.03.text: He said the poster doesn’t do me justice. He’s right, you know.
c7_gate.talk.stephen.2.03.speaker: stephen

c7_gate.talk.stephen.3.01.text: Rook’s copy wished you luck finding me.
c7_gate.talk.stephen.3.01.speaker: steve

c7_gate.talk.stephen.3.03.text: Please stop enjoying this so much.
c7_gate.talk.stephen.3.03.speaker: steve

c7_gate.talk.stephen.3.04.text: I can’t. This is the most fun I’ve had in my whole short life.
c7_gate.talk.stephen.3.04.speaker: stephen

c7_gate.truck.lead.03.text: The camera monitor shows the click the moment it leaves this desk.
c7_gate.truck.lead.03.speaker: shaw

c7_gate.truck.lead.04.text: The stage van shows the television feed. That runs two seconds late, because of the satellite.
c7_gate.truck.lead.04.speaker: shaw

c7_swap.bus.lead.02.text: Three sends. Amber reaches the lectern and the press van. Green reaches the back fence and the service steps.
c7_swap.bus.lead.02.speaker: shaw

c7_swap.bus.lead.03.text: Blue reaches the lectern, the back fence and the service steps.
c7_swap.bus.lead.03.speaker: shaw

c7_swap.bus.lead.05.text: For June’s reply, three returns. Copper goes to you, Stephen and the lectern speaker.
c7_swap.bus.lead.05.speaker: shaw

c7_swap.bus.lead.06.text: Slate goes to you and Stephen. Pearl goes to you alone.
c7_swap.bus.lead.06.speaker: shaw

c7_swap.bus.lead.07.text: June’s reply is for Stephen and me. Nobody else.
c7_swap.bus.lead.07.speaker: steve

c7_swap.map.lead.02.text: Iris said Ward’s own doctor scanned her weeks ago. A copy made back then can’t know about this morning.
c7_swap.map.lead.02.speaker: steve

c7_swap.map.lead.03.text: And this morning she burned her left wrist on the folder. Pell wrote it down. Left wrist, bandaged.
c7_swap.map.lead.03.speaker: stephen

c7_swap.map.lead.04.text: Podium camera. The woman at the lectern just waved. Her left wrist is bare.
c7_swap.map.lead.04.speaker: stephen

c7_swap.map.lead.05.text: Stair camera. The doctor is helping a patient down the east stair. Her left wrist is bandaged.
c7_swap.map.lead.05.speaker: stephen

c7_swap.map.lead.06.text: The east stair only goes to one door, into the service tunnel. And the lift went down empty.
c7_swap.map.lead.06.speaker: stephen

c7_swap.talk.calder.1.01.text: Iris is right beside me. She’s counting her steps out loud.
c7_swap.talk.calder.1.01.speaker: calder

c7_swap.talk.calder.1.02.text: Is she all right down there?
c7_swap.talk.calder.1.02.speaker: steve

c7_swap.talk.calder.1.03.text: She says she’s fine. She says it the way you always do.
c7_swap.talk.calder.1.03.speaker: calder

c7_swap.talk.shaw.1.01.text: The last time I sat at a desk out here, four generals stood behind me.
c7_swap.talk.shaw.1.01.speaker: shaw

c7_swap.talk.shaw.1.02.text: Were they as nervous as I am?
c7_swap.talk.shaw.1.02.speaker: steve

c7_swap.talk.shaw.1.03.text: Less. Breathe, Mercer. The tape won’t play any faster if you hold your breath.
c7_swap.talk.shaw.1.03.speaker: shaw

c7_swap.talk.shaw.2.01.text: Your father’s tape is in good shape. Who stored it?
c7_swap.talk.shaw.2.01.speaker: shaw

c7_swap.talk.shaw.2.02.text: He did. Cool and dry, and labeled in pencil. He labeled everything.
c7_swap.talk.shaw.2.02.speaker: steve

c7_swap.talk.shaw.2.03.text: Then I would have hired him in a heartbeat.
c7_swap.talk.shaw.2.03.speaker: shaw

c7_swap.talk.stephen.1.01.text: What did the press ask you?
c7_swap.talk.stephen.1.01.speaker: steve

c7_swap.talk.stephen.1.02.text: My favorite food. I said Sunday dinner at La Marea. Then I wasn’t sure whose memory that was.
c7_swap.talk.stephen.1.02.speaker: stephen

c7_swap.talk.stephen.1.03.text: It belongs to both of us. It was a good answer.
c7_swap.talk.stephen.1.03.speaker: steve

c7_swap.talk.stephen.2.01.text: My hands are shaking. Are yours shaking too?
c7_swap.talk.stephen.2.01.speaker: stephen

c7_swap.talk.stephen.2.02.text: They’ve been shaking since six this morning.
c7_swap.talk.stephen.2.02.speaker: steve

c7_swap.talk.stephen.2.03.text: Good. I was worried it was only me.
c7_swap.talk.stephen.2.03.speaker: stephen

c7_swap.tone.lead.03.text: The speakers switch to the anthem at eighteen seconds past. Your tone runs two seconds. It has to finish before then.
c7_swap.tone.lead.03.speaker: shaw

c8_beach.second.lead.02.text: I know every breath of her voicemail. Let me play it right next to this.
c8_beach.second.lead.02.speaker: steve

c8_lab.lastpage.lead.02.text: Three strokes. The second joins the first and climbs higher. Then a gap. Then a long stroke, lower than both.
c8_lab.lastpage.lead.02.speaker: wen

c8_lab.lastpage.lead.03.text: Dad wrote the pitch on every reel. A higher number means a higher note.
c8_lab.lastpage.lead.03.speaker: steve

c8_lab.notebook.lead.02.text: This scrap is the American test. Two drum strikes, a missing beat, then a lamp flare.
c8_lab.notebook.lead.02.speaker: wen

c8_lab.notebook.lead.03.text: This one is our test. Before we built it, we were sent a copy of the American test to study.
c8_lab.notebook.lead.03.speaker: wen

c8_lab.props.lead.02.text: Drums, lamps and fog. If two effects hit on the very same frames, one cue can drive them both.
c8_lab.props.lead.02.speaker: shaw

c8_lab.props.lead.03.text: Ignore anything marked rehearsal. That was me testing bulbs.
c8_lab.props.lead.03.speaker: shaw

c8_lab.talk.shaw.1.02.text: Six of them, from a laundromat in Reno. The owner thought I was starting a business.
c8_lab.talk.shaw.1.02.speaker: shaw

c8_lab.talk.shaw.2.01.text: Thirty years of explosions, and I can still hear a mouse cough in the next room.
c8_lab.talk.shaw.2.01.speaker: shaw

c8_lab.talk.shaw.2.02.text: So can I. It makes the cinema very hard.
c8_lab.talk.shaw.2.02.speaker: steve

c8_lab.talk.shaw.2.03.text: Sit in the back row. Nobody coughs in the back row.
c8_lab.talk.shaw.2.03.speaker: shaw

c8_lab.talk.wen.1.01.text: You knew my mother nine years ago. What was she like in that room?
c8_lab.talk.wen.1.01.speaker: steve

c8_lab.talk.wen.1.02.text: Tired, like all of us. But she brought a tin of lemon cookies and shared them with both sides.
c8_lab.talk.wen.1.02.speaker: wen

c8_lab.talk.wen.1.03.text: Nobody refuses a cookie from the interpreter. It was very clever of her.
c8_lab.talk.wen.1.03.speaker: wen

c8_lab.talk.wen.2.02.text: In Mandarin? Out here in Bellwether?
c8_lab.talk.wen.2.02.speaker: steve

c8_lab.talk.wen.2.03.text: Perfect Mandarin. Then she asked me if I needed any bait.
c8_lab.talk.wen.2.03.speaker: wen

c8_lab.talk.wen.3.02.text: Nine years. We were enemies for one week and friends ever since.
c8_lab.talk.wen.3.02.speaker: wen

c8_lab.talk.wen.3.03.text: She still owes me a dinner. She lost a bet about the fog machine.
c8_lab.talk.wen.3.03.speaker: wen

c8_rig.path.lead.03.text: The fleet trusts nothing that its own ship did not measure.
c8_rig.path.lead.03.speaker: wen

c8_rig.path.lead.05.text: And the sleepers are in the Gallery. Mom and Dad are in row nine.
c8_rig.path.lead.05.speaker: steve

c8_rig.rig.lead.02.text: I tested all three twice. Once to see the cue go out, and once to hear what leaks back.
c8_rig.rig.lead.02.speaker: wen

c8_rig.rig.lead.04.text: Careful. A dead coupler also lets nothing back. It looks perfect until you check the cue.
c8_rig.rig.lead.04.speaker: wen

c8_rig.source.lead.02.text: One jack carries my lamp tester. It flashes on beat five, every time.
c8_rig.source.lead.02.speaker: wen

c8_rig.source.lead.03.text: One carries my rehearsal film, looping on beat four. And one is my own hand on the button.
c8_rig.source.lead.03.speaker: shaw

c8_rig.source.lead.04.text: Shaw cued beat four, then beat seven. Birch flashed on five both times. Ash flashed on four both times.
c8_rig.source.lead.04.speaker: wen

c8_rig.source.lead.05.text: Elm flashed on four, then on seven. It followed her.
c8_rig.source.lead.05.speaker: wen

c8_rig.talk.iris.1.01.text: Did you water the balcony flowers before we left?
c8_rig.talk.iris.1.01.speaker: steve

c8_rig.talk.iris.1.02.text: This morning. The irises have two new buds. I counted them.
c8_rig.talk.iris.1.02.speaker: iris

c8_rig.talk.iris.1.03.text: Nora always forgot to water them. They nearly died twice.
c8_rig.talk.iris.1.03.speaker: steve

c8_rig.talk.iris.1.04.text: Then I’ll keep them alive until she’s home. That’s something I can do.
c8_rig.talk.iris.1.04.speaker: iris

c8_rig.talk.iris.2.01.text: Carmen called. She asked if we’re coming on Sunday. I told her yes, both of us.
c8_rig.talk.iris.2.01.speaker: iris

c8_rig.talk.iris.2.02.text: Both of us meaning you and me? Or Nora and me?
c8_rig.talk.iris.2.02.speaker: steve

c8_rig.talk.iris.2.03.text: Nora and you. I’ll be happy just to help set the plates.
c8_rig.talk.iris.2.03.speaker: iris

c8_rig.talk.iris.3.01.text: What have you lost so far?
c8_rig.talk.iris.3.01.speaker: steve

c8_rig.talk.iris.3.02.text: Small things. The name of Nora’s first goldfish. The way to her old school.
c8_rig.talk.iris.3.02.speaker: iris

c8_rig.talk.iris.3.03.text: It doesn’t hurt. It’s like a radio station drifting slowly out of range.
c8_rig.talk.iris.3.03.speaker: iris

c8_rig.talk.shaw.1.01.text: I’ve used eleven rolls of gaffer tape today. That’s a personal record.
c8_rig.talk.shaw.1.01.speaker: shaw

c8_rig.talk.shaw.1.02.text: Is that good news or bad news?
c8_rig.talk.shaw.1.02.speaker: steve

c8_rig.talk.shaw.1.03.text: In my business, it means the show is nearly ready.
c8_rig.talk.shaw.1.03.speaker: shaw

c8_rig.talk.stephen.1.01.text: I’m writing a list on my hand. Steve, Mom, Dad, Biscuit.
c8_rig.talk.stephen.1.01.speaker: stephen

c8_rig.talk.stephen.1.02.text: Biscuit made your list before the rest of the town?
c8_rig.talk.stephen.1.02.speaker: steve

c8_rig.talk.stephen.1.03.text: Biscuit is very important. Ask Pell.
c8_rig.talk.stephen.1.03.speaker: stephen

c8_rig.talk.stephen.2.01.text: When this is over, I’d like to do one show at the radio station. Just one.
c8_rig.talk.stephen.2.01.speaker: stephen

c8_rig.talk.stephen.2.02.text: The machine has my old chair now.
c8_rig.talk.stephen.2.02.speaker: steve

c8_rig.talk.stephen.2.03.text: Then we take it back together. You do the sound. I’ll do the talking.
c8_rig.talk.stephen.2.03.speaker: stephen

c8_rig.talk.ward.1.02.text: Bandaged and famous. Half the country has seen it on television.
c8_rig.talk.ward.1.02.speaker: ward

c8_rig.talk.ward.1.03.text: My doctor wants to look at it. I said, not you, thank you.
c8_rig.talk.ward.1.03.speaker: ward

c8_rig.talk.ward.2.01.text: A week ago I had never heard of Bellwether. Now I won’t forget it.
c8_rig.talk.ward.2.01.speaker: ward

c8_rig.talk.ward.2.02.text: Try Sunday dinner at La Marea before you leave. Carmen will feed you twice.
c8_rig.talk.ward.2.02.speaker: steve

c8_rig.talk.ward.2.03.text: If we’re all still here on Sunday, I’ll book a table.
c8_rig.talk.ward.2.03.speaker: ward

c8_rig.talk.wen.1.01.text: I called my daughter last night. She asked what I’m building this time.
c8_rig.talk.wen.1.01.speaker: wen

c8_rig.talk.wen.1.03.text: A very honest lie. She said that sounded exactly like me.
c8_rig.talk.wen.1.03.speaker: wen

c9_choir.talk.calder.1.01.text: Every door on this ship just opened at once.
c9_choir.talk.calder.1.01.speaker: calder

c9_choir.talk.calder.1.02.text: Is everybody all right down there?
c9_choir.talk.calder.1.02.speaker: steve

c9_choir.talk.calder.1.03.text: Dale Kittredge is asking for his mailbag. So yes, I think so.
c9_choir.talk.calder.1.03.speaker: calder

c9_choir.talk.frank.1.01.text: You kept a list, kiddo. Dates and everything.
c9_choir.talk.frank.1.01.speaker: frank

c9_choir.talk.frank.1.02.text: You taught me. Put a date on everything.
c9_choir.talk.frank.1.02.speaker: steve

c9_choir.talk.frank.1.03.text: I did, didn’t I? Good. I’m glad something stuck.
c9_choir.talk.frank.1.03.speaker: frank

c9_choir.talk.helen.1.01.text: It sings in phrases, like a person thinking out loud.
c9_choir.talk.helen.1.01.speaker: helen

c9_choir.talk.helen.1.02.text: Can you understand what it says?
c9_choir.talk.helen.1.02.speaker: steve

c9_choir.talk.helen.1.03.text: Not every word. But I can hear when it means something.
c9_choir.talk.helen.1.03.speaker: helen

c9_choir.talk.nora.1.01.text: Three hundred people just woke up in wet pajamas.
c9_choir.talk.nora.1.01.speaker: nora

c9_choir.talk.nora.1.02.text: And not one of them has shoes.
c9_choir.talk.nora.1.02.speaker: steve

c9_choir.talk.nora.1.03.text: I’m starting a line for blankets. Somebody has to.
c9_choir.talk.nora.1.03.speaker: nora

c9_choir.truth.lead.02.text: Nora’s good morning, on Saturday and on Sunday. The same breath, the same pause, both days.
c9_choir.truth.lead.02.speaker: steve

c9_choir.truth.lead.03.text: Rook telling June to sit tight. The same take on her voicemail and through a door in the mountains.
c9_choir.truth.lead.03.speaker: steve

c9_choir.truth.lead.04.text: And Iris, on Monday. She said the same words twice, and the second time she paused somewhere new.
c9_choir.truth.lead.04.speaker: steve

c9_choir.wick.lead.04.text: That’s the phrase from your father’s tapes. Two joined notes going up, a little gap, then one long low note.
c9_choir.wick.lead.04.speaker: helen

c9_choir.wick.lead.05.text: I wrote it in my margin, Steven. After the low note, it starts all over again.
c9_choir.wick.lead.05.speaker: helen

c9_gallery.antenna.lead.02.text: This visitor slip gets me onto the observation deck. It won’t open a single door.
c9_gallery.antenna.lead.02.speaker: calder

c9_gallery.antenna.lead.03.text: The lamp for the inner door is round the bend. You can only see it from the deck.
c9_gallery.antenna.lead.03.speaker: stephen

c9_gallery.antenna.lead.04.text: And I stay right here by Nora’s bed. I promised her.
c9_gallery.antenna.lead.04.speaker: steve

c9_gallery.antenna.lead.05.text: Then I don’t walk on until somebody sees that lamp light up.
c9_gallery.antenna.lead.05.speaker: stephen

c9_gallery.talk.calder.1.01.text: I took this slip from a sleeping man in a very nice suit.
c9_gallery.talk.calder.1.01.speaker: calder

c9_gallery.talk.calder.1.02.text: Is that strictly legal, Sheriff Calder?
c9_gallery.talk.calder.1.02.speaker: steve

c9_gallery.talk.calder.1.03.text: I’ll write myself a ticket when we get home.
c9_gallery.talk.calder.1.03.speaker: calder

c9_gallery.talk.calder.2.01.text: Adrian Rook is somewhere in this hall. The real one.
c9_gallery.talk.calder.2.01.speaker: calder

c9_gallery.talk.calder.2.02.text: We’ll find him, June. I promise.
c9_gallery.talk.calder.2.02.speaker: steve

c9_gallery.talk.calder.2.03.text: Good. He still owes me a coffee from twenty years ago.
c9_gallery.talk.calder.2.03.speaker: calder

c9_gallery.talk.guard.1.01.text: Would you like to be scanned while you wait?
c9_gallery.talk.guard.1.01.speaker: guard

c9_gallery.talk.guard.1.02.text: Still no, thank you. Very kind of you to ask again.
c9_gallery.talk.guard.1.02.speaker: steve

c9_gallery.talk.guard.1.03.text: Your answer has been noted. The offer remains open.
c9_gallery.talk.guard.1.03.speaker: guard

c9_gallery.talk.iris.1.01.text: You wore my favorite coat for five months.
c9_gallery.talk.iris.1.01.speaker: nora

c9_gallery.talk.iris.1.02.text: It is a good coat. I sewed the top button back on.
c9_gallery.talk.iris.1.02.speaker: iris

c9_gallery.talk.iris.1.03.text: I’ve been meaning to do that for two years.
c9_gallery.talk.iris.1.03.speaker: nora

c9_gallery.talk.iris.1.04.text: I know. I remembered meaning to.
c9_gallery.talk.iris.1.04.speaker: iris

c9_gallery.talk.iris.2.01.text: I keep reaching for things she knows. Some of them are already gone.
c9_gallery.talk.iris.2.01.speaker: iris

c9_gallery.talk.iris.2.02.text: Do you want me to stop asking you things?
c9_gallery.talk.iris.2.02.speaker: steve

c9_gallery.talk.iris.2.03.text: No. Keep asking. I want to find out which answers are mine.
c9_gallery.talk.iris.2.03.speaker: iris

c9_gallery.talk.nora.1.01.text: Did my mother notice? That it wasn’t me at her table?
c9_gallery.talk.nora.1.01.speaker: nora

c9_gallery.talk.nora.1.02.text: She said you’d stopped arguing with her. That’s how she knew something was wrong.
c9_gallery.talk.nora.1.02.speaker: steve

c9_gallery.talk.nora.1.03.text: Good. I’m going to argue with her all week.
c9_gallery.talk.nora.1.03.speaker: nora

c9_gallery.talk.nora.2.01.text: Is anybody feeding Admiral properly? He gets sulky.
c9_gallery.talk.nora.2.01.speaker: nora

c9_gallery.talk.nora.2.02.text: He stole my sandwich on the pier. Rye bread.
c9_gallery.talk.nora.2.02.speaker: steve

c9_gallery.talk.nora.2.03.text: He hates rye. He was making a point.
c9_gallery.talk.nora.2.03.speaker: nora

c9_gallery.talk.nora.2.04.text: He came to my whistle, Nor. Not hers. That’s when I started to wonder.
c9_gallery.talk.nora.2.04.speaker: steve

c9_gallery.talk.nora.3.01.text: I know half this hall by name now. It’s like a very cold party.
c9_gallery.talk.nora.3.01.speaker: nora

c9_gallery.talk.nora.3.02.text: Who is the best company down here?
c9_gallery.talk.nora.3.02.speaker: steve

c9_gallery.talk.nora.3.03.text: Dale Kittredge. He says he’s never been this late with the mail in thirty years.
c9_gallery.talk.nora.3.03.speaker: nora

c9_gallery.talk.stephen.1.02.text: Frank. Dad. I check it every few minutes. I hate that I have to.
c9_gallery.talk.stephen.1.02.speaker: stephen

c9_gallery.talk.stephen.1.03.text: Then I’ll check it with you. Every few minutes.
c9_gallery.talk.stephen.1.03.speaker: steve

c9_wake.agnes.02.text: Who has been minding my bait stall, Steven?
c9_wake.agnes.02.speaker: agnes_original

c9_wake.agnes.03.text: I thought you had, Mrs. Penhallow. Every Sunday on the pier.
c9_wake.agnes.03.speaker: steve

c9_wake.agnes.04.text: On Sundays? I never open on Sundays. Sunday is for church and the crossword.
c9_wake.agnes.04.speaker: agnes_original

c9_wake.agnes.lead.02.text: Her glasses case still has a price sticker from her bait shop. That one is hers.
c9_wake.agnes.lead.02.speaker: nora

c9_wake.talk.calder.1.01.text: He asked about his pajamas before he asked about me.
c9_wake.talk.calder.1.01.speaker: calder

c9_wake.talk.calder.1.02.text: He’s awake, June. That’s what matters.
c9_wake.talk.calder.1.02.speaker: steve

c9_wake.talk.calder.1.03.text: I know. I’m still telling everyone at the office.
c9_wake.talk.calder.1.03.speaker: calder

c9_wake.talk.frank.1.01.text: How long were we under, kiddo?
c9_wake.talk.frank.1.01.speaker: frank

c9_wake.talk.frank.1.02.text: Eighteen months, Dad. A year and a half.
c9_wake.talk.frank.1.02.speaker: steve

c9_wake.talk.frank.1.03.text: That’s a lot of Thursdays. The club must think I quit.
c9_wake.talk.frank.1.03.speaker: frank

c9_wake.talk.frank.1.04.text: They don’t. I called them on your radio. Gull nearly cried.
c9_wake.talk.frank.1.04.speaker: steve

c9_wake.talk.frank.2.01.text: Did the boat make it back?
c9_wake.talk.frank.2.01.speaker: frank

c9_wake.talk.frank.2.02.text: It drifted in the next morning. Your radio was still on.
c9_wake.talk.frank.2.02.speaker: steve

c9_wake.talk.frank.2.03.text: Good radio. I told your mother it was a good radio.
c9_wake.talk.frank.2.03.speaker: frank

c9_wake.talk.helen.1.01.text: You never told me the words, Mom.
c9_wake.talk.helen.1.01.speaker: steve

c9_wake.talk.helen.1.02.text: There weren’t any, Steven. I made up the tune your first night home from the hospital.
c9_wake.talk.helen.1.02.speaker: helen

c9_wake.talk.helen.1.03.text: The ship has been humming it for months.
c9_wake.talk.helen.1.03.speaker: steve

c9_wake.talk.helen.1.04.text: Then the ship has good taste.
c9_wake.talk.helen.1.04.speaker: helen

c9_wake.talk.helen.2.01.text: Is that Nora? She looks so tired.
c9_wake.talk.helen.2.01.speaker: helen

c9_wake.talk.helen.2.02.text: She ran this whole hall while you were asleep, Mom.
c9_wake.talk.helen.2.02.speaker: steve

c9_wake.talk.helen.2.03.text: Then she has earned a proper dinner. I’ll talk to Carmen.
c9_wake.talk.helen.2.03.speaker: helen

c9_wake.talk.nora.1.01.text: We kept this aisle open with a mop handle and a lot of shouting.
c9_wake.talk.nora.1.01.speaker: nora

c9_wake.talk.nora.1.03.text: Mostly mine. Dale helped. He shouts like a man who has met a lot of dogs.
c9_wake.talk.nora.1.03.speaker: nora

c9_wake.talk.nora.2.01.text: Your mother just asked me if I’m eating enough. On a spaceship.
c9_wake.talk.nora.2.01.speaker: nora

c9_wake.talk.nora.2.02.text: That’s how she says I love you.
c9_wake.talk.nora.2.02.speaker: steve

c9_wake.talk.nora.2.03.text: I know. My mother does the exact same thing with soup.
c9_wake.talk.nora.2.03.speaker: nora

c9_wake.talk.rook.1.01.text: Where are my clothes? Who has been wearing my clothes?
c9_wake.talk.rook.1.01.speaker: rook

c9_wake.talk.rook.1.02.text: A man with your face, Adrian. He had your manners too, mostly.
c9_wake.talk.rook.1.02.speaker: calder

c9_wake.talk.rook.1.03.text: Then he owes me a dry cleaning bill.
c9_wake.talk.rook.1.03.speaker: rook

epilogue.talk.agnes.1.01.text: The ship left without me, Steven. I asked it to.
epilogue.talk.agnes.1.01.speaker: agnes

epilogue.talk.agnes.1.03.text: I have the wind on a spool. I would miss the people more.
epilogue.talk.agnes.1.03.speaker: agnes

epilogue.talk.agnes_original.1.01.text: She charges ten cents less than me for worms. On purpose.
epilogue.talk.agnes_original.1.01.speaker: agnes_original

epilogue.talk.agnes_original.1.02.text: Somebody kept this stall open for three years, Agnes.
epilogue.talk.agnes_original.1.02.speaker: agnes

epilogue.talk.agnes_original.1.03.text: And in three years, nobody bought a single worm.
epilogue.talk.agnes_original.1.03.speaker: agnes_original

epilogue.talk.carmen.1.01.text: Six o’clock, Steve. Both of you. All of you.
epilogue.talk.carmen.1.01.speaker: carmen

epilogue.talk.carmen.1.02.text: You mean Iris is invited too?
epilogue.talk.carmen.1.02.speaker: steve

epilogue.talk.carmen.1.03.text: Iris too. She sat at my table for five months. Now she can help with the dishes.
epilogue.talk.carmen.1.03.speaker: carmen

epilogue.talk.carmen.2.01.text: I kept your plate warm every Sunday. This Monday I am not throwing it out.
epilogue.talk.carmen.2.01.speaker: carmen

epilogue.talk.carmen.2.02.text: You never had to keep it, Carmen.
epilogue.talk.carmen.2.02.speaker: steve

epilogue.talk.carmen.2.03.text: I know. That is why I did.
epilogue.talk.carmen.2.03.speaker: carmen

epilogue.talk.dale.1.01.text: First free morning in thirty years. No mailbag, and no frozen bed.
epilogue.talk.dale.1.01.speaker: dale

epilogue.talk.dale.1.02.text: What are you going to do instead, Dale?
epilogue.talk.dale.1.02.speaker: steve

epilogue.talk.dale.1.03.text: Sleep in a real bed. A warm one. Then go fishing.
epilogue.talk.dale.1.03.speaker: dale

epilogue.talk.gus.1.01.text: Try it, Steve. It’s green, but it’s honest.
epilogue.talk.gus.1.01.speaker: gus

epilogue.talk.gus.1.02.text: Gus, this is actually really good.
epilogue.talk.gus.1.02.speaker: steve

epilogue.talk.gus.1.03.text: Don’t tell anyone. I have a reputation for plain bread.
epilogue.talk.gus.1.03.speaker: gus

epilogue.talk.helen.1.02.text: Is the kettle actually labeled now?
epilogue.talk.helen.1.02.speaker: steve

epilogue.talk.helen.1.03.text: Kettle. In capital letters. I married a very thorough man.
epilogue.talk.helen.1.03.speaker: helen

epilogue.talk.helen.2.01.text: I keep hearing Wick’s phrase when I do the dishes.
epilogue.talk.helen.2.01.speaker: helen

epilogue.talk.helen.2.03.text: I never stopped, Steven. For a while I just had nobody to translate for.
epilogue.talk.helen.2.03.speaker: helen

epilogue.talk.iris.1.01.text: I chose this face myself. It’s strange to be surprised by a mirror.
epilogue.talk.iris.1.01.speaker: iris

epilogue.talk.iris.1.02.text: It suits you. It really does.
epilogue.talk.iris.1.02.speaker: steve

epilogue.talk.iris.1.03.text: Nora says the nose is too serious. I think that means she likes it.
epilogue.talk.iris.1.03.speaker: iris

epilogue.talk.iris.2.01.text: Carmen invited me to dinner on Sunday. Is that a trap?
epilogue.talk.iris.2.01.speaker: iris

epilogue.talk.iris.2.02.text: With Carmen, dinner and a trap can be the same thing.
epilogue.talk.iris.2.02.speaker: steve

epilogue.talk.iris.2.03.text: Then I’ll bring bread. Nora says bread is always safe.
epilogue.talk.iris.2.03.speaker: iris

epilogue.talk.lyle.1.01.text: Ben has the school play tonight. He wants both of us in the front row.
epilogue.talk.lyle.1.01.speaker: lyle

epilogue.talk.lyle.1.02.text: Two Lyle Boones in one front row.
epilogue.talk.lyle.1.02.speaker: steve

epilogue.talk.lyle.1.03.text: The other one learned the lines with him. I’m still learning mine.
epilogue.talk.lyle.1.03.speaker: lyle

epilogue.talk.lyle_copy.1.01.text: I still go to every game. Now we take turns driving.
epilogue.talk.lyle_copy.1.01.speaker: lyle_copy

epilogue.talk.lyle_copy.1.02.text: He’s better at the snacks. I’m better at yelling at the umpire.
epilogue.talk.lyle_copy.1.02.speaker: lyle

epilogue.talk.lyle_copy.1.03.text: We’re working on that. Both of us.
epilogue.talk.lyle_copy.1.03.speaker: lyle_copy

epilogue.talk.nora.1.01.text: I go back to the aquarium on Monday. The otter pups won’t remember me.
epilogue.talk.nora.1.01.speaker: nora

epilogue.talk.nora.1.02.text: They’ll remember you. You’re the one who argues with the vet.
epilogue.talk.nora.1.02.speaker: steve

epilogue.talk.nora.1.03.text: Everybody argues with the vet. I just win.
epilogue.talk.nora.1.03.speaker: nora

epilogue.talk.nora.2.01.text: Somebody rearranged our kitchen. Everything is in alphabetical order.
epilogue.talk.nora.2.01.speaker: nora

epilogue.talk.nora.2.02.text: That was Iris. She thought it looked tidy.
epilogue.talk.nora.2.02.speaker: steve

epilogue.talk.nora.2.03.text: The forks are under F. I’m leaving them there. It makes me laugh every morning.
epilogue.talk.nora.2.03.speaker: nora

epilogue.talk.nora.3.01.text: Admiral came to my whistle this morning. Straight out of the water.
epilogue.talk.nora.3.01.speaker: nora

epilogue.talk.nora.3.02.text: Your second note went up again. I heard it from the pier.
epilogue.talk.nora.3.02.speaker: steve

epilogue.talk.nora.3.03.text: It always went up, Steve. Somebody else was whistling it wrong.
epilogue.talk.nora.3.03.speaker: nora

epilogue.talk.pell.1.01.text: Biscuit knows every porch on the route. I am still learning the gates.
epilogue.talk.pell.1.01.speaker: pell

epilogue.talk.pell.1.02.text: The blue gate on Harbor Street sticks. Kick it low.
epilogue.talk.pell.1.02.speaker: dale

epilogue.talk.pell.1.03.text: Kick it low. I have written that down.
epilogue.talk.pell.1.03.speaker: pell

epilogue.talk.rook.1.01.text: I have a lot of reports to write. Nobody is going to believe them.
epilogue.talk.rook.1.01.speaker: rook

epilogue.talk.rook.1.02.text: Write them anyway, Adrian. Every word.
epilogue.talk.rook.1.02.speaker: steve

epilogue.talk.rook.1.03.text: That’s what June said. Word for word.
epilogue.talk.rook.1.03.speaker: rook

epilogue.talk.rook_copy.1.02.text: Good luck out there. I mean it.
epilogue.talk.rook_copy.1.02.speaker: steve

epilogue.talk.rook_copy.1.03.text: Tell June I’m sorry about the voicemail.
epilogue.talk.rook_copy.1.03.speaker: rook_copy

i1_archive.quiet.lead.02.text: Seven worlds with people on them. Every one went quiet soon after the fleet arrived.
i1_archive.quiet.lead.02.speaker: archivist

i1_archive.quiet.lead.04.text: The sleeper in Row Zero came aboard three hundred years ago. It has never said a word.
i1_archive.quiet.lead.04.speaker: archivist

i1_archive.reset.lead.02.text: The law is simple. The source is never touched. The echo is restored from the source.
i1_archive.reset.lead.02.speaker: archivist

i1_archive.reset.lead.03.text: And whatever the echo loses, I must describe in the witness ledger. In words, not numbers.
i1_archive.reset.lead.03.speaker: archivist

i1_archive.signals.lead.03.text: Each pulse has one missing beat near the middle. And each station wrote down when its lamp flared.
i1_archive.signals.lead.03.speaker: archivist

i1_archive.talk.gus.1.01.text: Tell me about your bakery, Gus Albano.
i1_archive.talk.gus.1.01.speaker: archivist

i1_archive.talk.gus.1.02.text: Ovens on at four. The radio on, low. My grandmother’s recipes, every one of them.
i1_archive.talk.gus.1.02.speaker: gus

i1_archive.talk.gus.1.03.text: People wait outside in the rain for her cinnamon knots.
i1_archive.talk.gus.1.03.speaker: gus

i1_archive.talk.gus.1.04.text: Then they must be very good knots.
i1_archive.talk.gus.1.04.speaker: archivist

i1_archive.talk.gus.2.01.text: What do the people of your town do in the morning?
i1_archive.talk.gus.2.01.speaker: archivist

i1_archive.talk.gus.2.02.text: They buy bread and complain about the weather. Then most of them buy a second loaf.
i1_archive.talk.gus.2.02.speaker: gus

i1_archive.talk.gus.2.03.text: Why would anyone need a second loaf?
i1_archive.talk.gus.2.03.speaker: archivist

i1_archive.talk.gus.2.04.text: For a neighbor. Everybody there has somebody to bring bread to.
i1_archive.talk.gus.2.04.speaker: gus

i1_archive.talk.gus.3.01.text: Have you seen my delivery van? It has a giant croissant on the roof.
i1_archive.talk.gus.3.01.speaker: gus

i1_archive.talk.gus.3.02.text: I have not. Is the croissant necessary?
i1_archive.talk.gus.3.02.speaker: archivist

i1_archive.talk.gus.3.03.text: Absolutely. Children wave at it. Nobody waves at a plain van.
i1_archive.talk.gus.3.03.speaker: gus

i1_archive.talk.gus.4.01.text: Do you remember the croissant, Gus?
i1_archive.talk.gus.4.01.speaker: archivist

i1_archive.talk.gus.4.02.text: Croissant? I bake my grandmother’s recipes. I have never changed one.
i1_archive.talk.gus.4.02.speaker: gus

i1_archive.talk.gus.4.03.text: No. Of course you have not. Go back to your ovens.
i1_archive.talk.gus.4.03.speaker: archivist

i2_nora.pump.lead.02.text: The top dial reads an empty wash line. Ignore it. Watch the return and the bed flow.
i2_nora.pump.lead.02.speaker: nora

i2_nora.pump.lead.03.text: Bed flow has to stay at three or more. The return has to drop below three.
i2_nora.pump.lead.03.speaker: nora

i2_nora.talk.dale.1.02.text: Cold, stiff and starving. If this is a hospital, the food is terrible.
i2_nora.talk.dale.1.02.speaker: dale

i2_nora.talk.dale.1.03.text: There isn’t any food here, Dale.
i2_nora.talk.dale.1.03.speaker: nora

i2_nora.talk.dale.1.04.text: That is exactly my point, Nora.
i2_nora.talk.dale.1.04.speaker: dale

i2_nora.talk.dale.2.01.text: Who is feeding June Calder’s beagle? I carry biscuits in my bag for her every morning.
i2_nora.talk.dale.2.01.speaker: dale

i2_nora.talk.dale.2.02.text: I’m sure somebody is looking after Biscuit.
i2_nora.talk.dale.2.02.speaker: nora

i2_nora.talk.dale.2.03.text: Somebody had better be. She sulks at anyone who forgets.
i2_nora.talk.dale.2.03.speaker: dale

i2_nora.talk.dale.3.01.text: Left at the pipes, right at the cold one, straight past the humming wall.
i2_nora.talk.dale.3.01.speaker: dale

i2_nora.talk.dale.3.02.text: You really did learn the whole route.
i2_nora.talk.dale.3.02.speaker: nora

i2_nora.talk.dale.3.03.text: Mail carriers never forget a route, Nora. We only forget birthdays.
i2_nora.talk.dale.3.03.speaker: dale

i2_nora.talk.lyle.1.01.text: My boys have a game on Saturday. I’ve missed most of their games this year.
