i2_nora.talk.lyle.1.01.speaker: lyle

i2_nora.talk.lyle.1.02.text: Then you’ll make the next one, Lyle.
i2_nora.talk.lyle.1.02.speaker: nora

i2_nora.talk.lyle.1.03.text: Every single one, when I get out of here. I swear it.
i2_nora.talk.lyle.1.03.speaker: lyle

i2_nora.talk.lyle.2.01.text: I should be at work. Somebody must be covering my shifts.
i2_nora.talk.lyle.2.01.speaker: lyle

i2_nora.talk.lyle.2.02.text: I think somebody probably is, Lyle.
i2_nora.talk.lyle.2.02.speaker: nora

i2_nora.talk.lyle.2.03.text: Then I hope he’s nicer to Steve Mercer than I was.
i2_nora.talk.lyle.2.03.speaker: lyle

one_year.in.04.text: Coffee for the morning hosts. Black, too strong, one for each of you.
one_year.in.04.speaker: nora

one_year.talk.nora.1.01.text: One year since the ninth night. Do you want to do something special?
one_year.talk.nora.1.01.speaker: nora

one_year.talk.nora.1.02.text: Coffee, and a real conversation. Same as every other day.
one_year.talk.nora.1.02.speaker: steve

one_year.talk.nora.1.03.text: Good answer. I was testing you.
one_year.talk.nora.1.03.speaker: nora

one_year.talk.nora.2.01.text: People keep asking about my ring. I tell them it’s a long story with a spaceship in it.
one_year.talk.nora.2.01.speaker: nora

one_year.talk.nora.2.02.text: It is a long story with a spaceship in it.
one_year.talk.nora.2.02.speaker: steve

one_year.talk.nora.2.03.text: I know. That’s why I love telling it.
one_year.talk.nora.2.03.speaker: nora

one_year.talk.nora.3.01.text: Admiral has a girlfriend now. She’s very loud, and she argues with everybody.
one_year.talk.nora.3.01.speaker: nora

one_year.talk.nora.3.02.text: That sounds like someone I know.
one_year.talk.nora.3.02.speaker: steve

one_year.talk.nora.3.03.text: Careful, Mercer. I still argue with everybody too.
one_year.talk.nora.3.03.speaker: nora

one_year.talk.stephen.1.01.text: People still ask which of us is the original. I tell them I’m the morning one.
one_year.talk.stephen.1.01.speaker: stephen

one_year.talk.stephen.1.02.text: I’m the morning one. You came in at noon yesterday.
one_year.talk.stephen.1.02.speaker: steve

one_year.talk.stephen.1.03.text: You see? This is why we need a segment.
one_year.talk.stephen.1.03.speaker: stephen

one_year.talk.stephen.2.01.text: Dad wants both of us on the club radio this Thursday.
one_year.talk.stephen.2.01.speaker: stephen

one_year.talk.stephen.2.02.text: He made us matching mugs for it, too.
one_year.talk.stephen.2.02.speaker: steve

one_year.talk.tomas.1.01.text: Episode one. I already have three apologies lined up.
one_year.talk.tomas.1.01.speaker: tomas

one_year.talk.tomas.1.02.text: Who is apologizing to you, Tomás?
one_year.talk.tomas.1.02.speaker: steve

one_year.talk.tomas.1.03.text: The Sheriff, the mayor and my mother. My mother is still thinking about it.
one_year.talk.tomas.1.03.speaker: tomas

one_year.talk.tomas.2.01.text: I said it was nine nights. On my podcast. Every week. Everybody laughed.
one_year.talk.tomas.2.01.speaker: tomas

one_year.talk.tomas.2.02.text: You’re the one laughing now. Constantly. In our booth.
one_year.talk.tomas.2.02.speaker: stephen

p_meeting.confess.lead.02.text: Our observers saw a ring of light on your screen. We were never allowed inside your room.
p_meeting.confess.lead.02.speaker: general_us

p_meeting.confess.lead.03.text: Our observers saw a ring of light on yours. We never went inside your room either.
p_meeting.confess.lead.03.speaker: general_cn

p_meeting.confess.lead.04.text: Each man could only speak for his own machine. And the joint minutes would be read by the whole world.
p_meeting.confess.lead.04.speaker: helen

p_meeting.talk.general_cn.1.01.text: Your building has no windows, Mrs. Mercer. And no tea.
p_meeting.talk.general_cn.1.01.speaker: general_cn

p_meeting.talk.general_cn.1.02.text: I brought my own. Jasmine. There is enough for two.
p_meeting.talk.general_cn.1.02.speaker: helen

p_meeting.talk.general_cn.1.03.text: Then this meeting has already gone better than I expected.
p_meeting.talk.general_cn.1.03.speaker: general_cn

p_meeting.talk.general_cn.2.01.text: You choose your words very carefully. Who taught you?
p_meeting.talk.general_cn.2.01.speaker: general_cn

p_meeting.talk.general_cn.2.02.text: My mother. Now my son corrects me. He records everything, even the kettle.
p_meeting.talk.general_cn.2.02.speaker: helen

p_meeting.talk.general_cn.2.03.text: A family of listeners. That is rare these days.
p_meeting.talk.general_cn.2.03.speaker: general_cn

p_meeting.talk.general_us.1.01.text: Coffee, General? It comes from the machine in the hall.
p_meeting.talk.general_us.1.01.speaker: helen

p_meeting.talk.general_us.1.02.text: Is it any good, Mrs. Mercer?
p_meeting.talk.general_us.1.02.speaker: general_us

p_meeting.talk.general_us.1.03.text: No. But it is hot, and it doesn’t pretend to be anything else.
p_meeting.talk.general_us.1.03.speaker: helen

p_meeting.talk.general_us.2.01.text: We put our test out on open radio. Every ham in three states heard it.
p_meeting.talk.general_us.2.01.speaker: general_us

p_meeting.talk.general_us.2.02.text: My husband is a ham. He talked about it at dinner for a week.
p_meeting.talk.general_us.2.02.speaker: helen

p_meeting.terms.lead.02.text: My card had two words he might use. One meant a technical demonstration. The other meant a performance, as on a stage.
p_meeting.terms.lead.02.speaker: helen

p_meeting.terms.lead.03.text: My rule never changes. An interpreter adds nothing and removes nothing.
p_meeting.terms.lead.03.speaker: helen

p_veyr.levels.lead.01.text: The gusts so far touched minus nine, minus three and minus six on the meter.
p_veyr.levels.lead.01.speaker: archivist

p_veyr.levels.lead.02.text: The engines will be nine decibels louder than the loudest gust. Above zero, the meter turns red.
p_veyr.levels.lead.02.speaker: archivist

postcredits.talk.helen.1.01.text: I kept page twelve by my bed for a year. Just in case.
postcredits.talk.helen.1.01.speaker: helen

postcredits.talk.helen.1.02.text: Lucky for us that you did.
postcredits.talk.helen.1.02.speaker: shaw

postcredits.talk.helen.1.03.text: Not luck. An interpreter always keeps the last page.
postcredits.talk.helen.1.03.speaker: helen

postcredits.talk.shaw.1.01.text: I run this listening station now. No fog machines. Real antennas.
postcredits.talk.shaw.1.01.speaker: shaw

postcredits.talk.shaw.1.02.text: I signed that budget. I still don’t fully understand it.
postcredits.talk.shaw.1.02.speaker: ward

postcredits.talk.shaw.1.03.text: Nobody does. That’s how you know it’s real science.
postcredits.talk.shaw.1.03.speaker: shaw

postcredits.talk.ward.1.01.text: Do you know how many people I had to wake up to get here?
postcredits.talk.ward.1.01.speaker: ward

postcredits.talk.ward.1.02.text: All of them, I hope. They’ll want to hear this.
postcredits.talk.ward.1.02.speaker: shaw

c10_live.first.lead.01.text: Orchard is listening for you, Steve. The pier is watching Orchard.
c10_live.first.lead.01.speaker: nora

c10_station.talk.stephen.1.02.text: You do. Black and very strong, two cups before breakfast.
c10_station.talk.stephen.1.02.speaker: steve

c10_town.talk.wen.1.03.text: It did not. My test fooled two admirals as well.
c10_town.talk.wen.1.03.speaker: wen

c2_ship.escape.lead.03.text: Two speaker covers by my hand. The attendant tested the hall speakers on the cracked one.
c2_ship.escape.lead.03.speaker: steve

c4_safe.screens.02.text: And a list of placements in Washington and Beijing. The first name on it is Walt, from June’s list.
c4_safe.screens.02.speaker: steve

c5_shack.notes.lead.02.text: Coltrane was Dad’s favorite record. And weather carts are the little weather tapes we played on air at KBWR.
c5_shack.notes.lead.02.speaker: steve

c5_shack.rig.lead.03.text: Dad’s rule for packs. Same volts, same center pin, and at least as much current as the card asks for.
c5_shack.rig.lead.03.speaker: steve

c6_jail.talk.pell.1.01.text: How is Biscuit doing these days?
c6_jail.talk.pell.1.01.speaker: steve

c6_jail.talk.pell.2.03.text: I have started to like a twelfth. Carmen gives me a churro at La Marea. The real Dale never stopped there.
c6_jail.talk.pell.2.03.speaker: pell

c7_gate.talk.pell.1.01.text: Who is looking after Biscuit today?
c7_gate.talk.pell.1.01.speaker: steve

c7_swap.tone.lead.02.text: The team gets to the patient at 11:58 and fourteen seconds. Not one second sooner.
c7_swap.tone.lead.02.speaker: calder

c8_lab.talk.wen.3.01.text: How long have you two known each other?
c8_lab.talk.wen.3.01.speaker: steve

c8_rig.path.lead.02.text: The dock receipt says a camera saw the lamps. The mast receipt says the ship measured them. The shore receipt says the ship got our crew’s numbers.
c8_rig.path.lead.02.speaker: wen

c8_rig.rig.lead.03.text: We need a signal going out and nothing coming back. Otherwise the ship hears my theater.
c8_rig.rig.lead.03.speaker: shaw

c9_wake.agnes.lead.03.text: The row list says the sleeper marked OT is on her left, and MV is on her right.
c9_wake.agnes.lead.03.speaker: nora

c9_wake.talk.nora.1.02.text: All that shouting? I can believe that.
c9_wake.talk.nora.1.02.speaker: steve

epilogue.talk.agnes.1.02.text: Won’t you miss the wind back home?
epilogue.talk.agnes.1.02.speaker: steve

epilogue.talk.helen.1.01.text: Your father leaves me a note every morning now. Today’s note says the kettle is labeled.
epilogue.talk.helen.1.01.speaker: helen

i1_archive.quiet.lead.03.text: The newest went quiet three hundred years ago. The other six went quiet at least five hundred years ago.
i1_archive.quiet.lead.03.speaker: archivist

p_meeting.talk.general_us.2.03.text: Then I hope your husband enjoyed the show.
p_meeting.talk.general_us.2.03.speaker: general_us

c2_aquarium.intercom.lead.02.text: The paper on the spool is dated in her handwriting. May 29th.
c2_aquarium.intercom.lead.02.speaker: steve

c4_escape.ctx.03.text: The van for my transfer was already parked in the transport bay, keys in it, waiting for five o’clock.
c4_escape.ctx.03.speaker: steve

c4_escape.fault.02.text: The bells went off in every room. Agents in socks. Somebody holding a toothbrush. And by the rules, the witness and his escort went first, in the five o’clock van, six hours early.
c4_escape.fault.02.speaker: steve

c4_escape.fault.find.text: A BLUE drill, for real, on the escort’s own ticket. The whole west corridor, me included, goes to the transport bay, and the rules put me straight into my own transfer van. Rook stays in the east wing with June.
c4_escape.fault.find.speaker: steve

c4_escape.fault.lead.04.text: The house rules are pinned above it. In any alarm, a protected witness leaves in his assigned vehicle, with his assigned escort. Mine is the five o’clock van.
c4_escape.fault.lead.04.speaker: steve

c4_escape.out.03.text: Roadblocks on the coast road and both bridges. Dogs at first light. He’ll head for town.
c4_escape.out.03.speaker: rook_copy

c4_escape.out.04.text: So I didn’t. I turned the radio off, went down the creek bed instead of the road, and walked all night toward the one place nobody had opened in eighteen months.
c4_escape.out.04.speaker: steve

c4_escape.recap.02.text: Now I was in a ditch in the hills above the bay with Dad’s recorder, a stolen radio and no plan. And the radio was still talking.
c4_escape.recap.02.speaker: steve

c4_escape.van.lead.04.text: We were on the old logging road down toward Bellwether. Rook would hear about the drill within minutes. I had less than that.
c4_escape.van.lead.04.speaker: steve

c4_safe.ctx.02.text: He drove us to a Bureau safe house in the hills above the bay. An hour from town, with nobody else for miles.
c4_safe.ctx.02.speaker: steve

c4_safe.out.04.text: At five o’clock a van takes you down to Bellwether. You’ll be processed at the Sheriff’s office. It’s only paperwork.
c4_safe.out.04.speaker: rook_copy

c4_safe.out.05.text: Bellwether. Where the ship is. I had a feeling I would never get as far as the paperwork.
c4_safe.out.05.speaker: steve

c5_shack.ctx.01.text: By sunrise my face was on every wanted poster in the county. I came down out of the trees to Dad’s radio shack, on the bluff above the bay.
c5_shack.ctx.01.speaker: steve

c5_station.out.05.text: You woke up on the ship.
c5_station.out.05.speaker: steve

c5_station.out.08.text: Carmen saw you at the market.
c5_station.out.08.speaker: steve

c5_station.out.09.text: She hugged me and said I looked well. I didn’t know why that made me want to cry. After that I watched June’s house all week. Today I followed you up the path to Dad’s shack. Twice.
c5_station.out.09.speaker: stephen

c5_station.out.10.text: Then I heard you through the shack window. The good stuff, the station library. So I came here first, and waited for you in the dark.
c5_station.out.10.speaker: stephen

c5_station.out.11.text: Then the earpiece in his hand clicked. I knew that voice. It was the one on the ship’s intercom, the one that opened my chair.
c5_station.out.11.speaker: steve

c5_station.out.12.text: Hunter. You missed your report. Where is the original?
c5_station.out.12.speaker: saren

c5_station.out.13.text: Stephen looked at me for a long time. Then he lifted the earpiece to his ear.
c5_station.out.13.speaker: steve

c5_station.out.14.text: Not at the station. He’s gone north, toward the border. I’m following him.
c5_station.out.14.speaker: stephen

c5_station.out.15.text: There. I’ve just lied to a spaceship for you. I think that makes us brothers.
c5_station.out.15.speaker: stephen

c5_station.stephen.find.text: He remembers Mom’s chipped jam jar, and nothing of home after that breakfast. He doesn’t know about the boat. He doesn’t know they’re gone.
c5_station.stephen.find.speaker: steve

c5_station.stephen.lead.03.text: The last thing I remember of home is breakfast in Dad’s shack. Mom’s jam jar, with the chip in the blue lid.
c5_station.stephen.lead.03.speaker: stephen

c6_iris.ctx.01.text: Stephen and I spent the weekend in Dad’s shack, arguing about haircuts. Every night at nine, he told the earpiece I’d gone north.
c6_iris.ctx.01.speaker: steve

c6_iris.out.04.text: She took a flat paper envelope out of her coat. Inside was one of the irises I knocked off the balcony on the ninth night, pressed flat.
c6_iris.out.04.speaker: steve

c6_iris.out.05.text: I picked it up after you ran. It is the first thing I ever kept that nobody told me to keep.
c6_iris.out.05.speaker: iris

c6_iris.out.08.text: It came out a little different the second time. Nothing a recording would ever do.
c6_iris.out.08.speaker: steve

c6_jail.crossword.01.text: Twenty-three across. Inimitable. Unlike my colleague on the radio.
c6_jail.crossword.01.speaker: calder

c6_jail.crossword.03.text: Radio June said T. Close. Wrong.
c6_jail.crossword.03.speaker: steve

c6_jail.crossword.lead.03.text: I’ll ask them both which letter I circled today. Only one of them has seen it.
c6_jail.crossword.lead.03.speaker: steve

c6_jail.mail.03.text: Twenty-three across, where it crosses eight down. Only the woman in cell two will see that square.
c6_jail.mail.03.speaker: steve

c6_jail.mail.find.text: The key was in the Jail drawer, slot 9, where entries 17 and 18 share a slot. And on June’s crossword I circled the square where 23 Across crosses 8 Down. Only the woman in cell two will see it.
c6_jail.mail.find.speaker: steve

c6_jail.mail.lead.06.text: County rule. When a cell is used, the spare key goes back to the clerk by registered post. The Sheriff wrote that rule. Her copy follows it exactly.
c6_jail.mail.lead.06.speaker: pell

c7_gate.in.03.text: We spent Tuesday in the back room of Gus’s bakery, planning on flour sacks.
c7_gate.in.03.speaker: steve

c7_gate.in.04.text: We couldn’t call anyone. The FBI’s man at the signing was Rook’s copy, and Rook’s list had names in Washington.
c7_gate.in.04.speaker: steve

c7_gate.in.05.text: So we used what we had. Halcyon runs the sound for the signing, Stephen still has their crew pass, and Dad’s tape has the tone.
c7_gate.in.05.speaker: steve

c7_gate.in.06.text: June wrote to the President in her own hand. Pell would deliver it the way he delivers everything: into the right hand, on time.
c7_gate.in.06.speaker: steve

c7_gate.in.07.text: Gus had two catering passes for the press tent. June and Iris would use them at the red window, at ten past eleven, on foot, in his aprons and hairnets, carrying croissants.
c7_gate.in.07.speaker: steve

c7_gate.recap.03.text: June and Iris were already inside, in hairnets, somewhere near the service tunnel. Iris knew the crew’s routes. She used to walk them.
c7_gate.recap.03.speaker: steve

c7_swap.ctx.03.text: At ten to twelve, the earpiece in Stephen’s hand stopped asking him for reports. It asked for me, by name.
c7_swap.ctx.03.speaker: steve

c7_swap.tone.04.text: She has my letter. She read it by flashlight in the tunnel, and she believes us. She wants to meet the man at the sound desk.
c7_swap.tone.04.speaker: calder

c5_station.out.07.text: Find the man with my face. Find Mom’s notebook. Report in every single night.
c5_station.out.07.speaker: stephen

c1_escape.cross.find.text: She was close enough to stop me. She didn’t move.
c1_escape.cross.find.speaker: steve

c1_escape.ctx.02.text: Her raincoat was dripping on the floor. I carried it out to hang on the balcony hooks.
c1_escape.ctx.02.speaker: steve

c1_escape.in.02.text: Nora? The balcony door’s locked. From inside.
c1_escape.in.02.speaker: steve

c1_escape.power.lead.01.text: Mr. Bell’s gate. It’s the only way down from here.
c1_escape.power.lead.01.speaker: steve

c5_station.out.16.text: Then tell me one thing, brother. Why didn’t they send copies of Mom and Dad home, the way they sent Nora’s?
c5_station.out.16.speaker: steve

c5_station.out.17.text: The tall man said Mom’s scan was damaged. A copy of her wouldn’t know where the notebook is. And the town had already buried them. The empty boat came back.
c5_station.out.17.speaker: stephen

c5_station.out.18.text: So they keep them asleep. As long as Mom sleeps, the notebook has an owner they can ask.
c5_station.out.18.speaker: stephen

c5_station.stephen.lead.01.text: ...The man Carmen saw at the market. My face.
c5_station.stephen.lead.01.speaker: steve

c6_iris.alibi.02.text: By the time an officer reached the bread window, Stephen was out through the alley.
c6_iris.alibi.02.speaker: steve

c6_iris.out.06.text: I hid in the otter house from Tuesday until last night. If they catch me again, they will reset me, and I won’t remember any of this. Not even that I chose a name.
c6_iris.out.06.speaker: iris

c6_iris.out.09.text: Last night the crew found me. They took me below to be reset, and left me on a laundry cart in the Gallery while the shift bell rang.
c6_iris.out.09.speaker: iris

c6_iris.out.10.text: Nora was in the third bed. Lyle Boone and Dale were beside her. I set their beds to a slow wake. It is gentle, and it can be undone.
c6_iris.out.10.speaker: iris

c6_iris.out.11.text: It finishes tonight, so someone inside will be awake when you come. Then I rode out with the wash.
c6_iris.out.11.speaker: iris

c6_iris.out.12.text: Steve didn’t take me. I’ll say it where the whole market can hear.
c6_iris.out.12.speaker: iris

c6_iris.out.13.text: She said it at the fish stalls, in Nora’s coat, loud enough for half the market. An officer heard it too. By the time he reached for his radio, she was gone.
c6_iris.out.13.speaker: steve

c6_iris.recap.03.text: And she told me about June. They scanned her at the safe house. Her copy has run the Sheriff’s office since Friday, and the real June is locked in her own cell until the ninth night.
c6_iris.recap.03.speaker: steve

c6_iris.recap.04.text: She also told me who could get us inside: the mail carrier. The spare key to June’s cell went back through the post. “He isn’t Dale,” she said. “But he loves June’s dog.”
c6_iris.recap.04.speaker: steve

c6_jail.crossword.04.text: Stay right there, Mercer. I’m on my way in.
c6_jail.crossword.04.speaker: calder

c6_jail.crossword.05.text: She knows my files. She doesn’t know me. Back door, Mercer.
c6_jail.crossword.05.speaker: calder

c6_jail.crossword.06.text: Pell held the back door. When her patrol car pulled up out front, we were already behind Gus’s bakery.
c6_jail.crossword.06.speaker: steve

c6_jail.crossword.find.text: The June in cell two had my crossword in her hand: the M where 23 Across crosses 8 Down. The June on the radio guessed a T, so she has never been near that cell. Iris was right. I unlocked cell two, and we left by the back before her copy reached the front.
c6_jail.crossword.find.speaker: steve

c6_jail.crossword.lead.02.text: Check my paperwork, Mercer. I taught you that.
c6_jail.crossword.lead.02.speaker: calder

c6_jail.ctx.01.text: The Sheriff’s office, just before four. Since Iris spoke up at the market, the search for Nora was over. June’s copy and Lyle’s copy were out on the harbor, calling the boats in.
c6_jail.ctx.01.speaker: steve

c6_jail.ctx.02.text: Stephen and Iris waited behind Gus’s bakery next door. I walked in the front door. Pell was sorting the afternoon mail.
c6_jail.ctx.02.speaker: steve

c6_jail.in.03.text: Maybe we should put the dog in charge.
c6_jail.in.03.speaker: steve

c6_jail.in.04.text: All boats, stand down. Nora Reyes is safe. The search is closed.
c6_jail.in.04.speaker: calder

c6_jail.mail.04.text: Then I’ll call the Sheriff on the desk radio. Both Junes get the same question.
c6_jail.mail.04.speaker: steve

c6_jail.out.06.text: By dark the posters were back up, with a new charge from Rook’s copy: Steve Mercer, fled federal custody. June’s copy knew who had opened cell two.
c6_jail.out.06.speaker: steve

c6_jail.recap.01.text: June is out of her cell. Her copy knows I was there, and that I let June out. Pell chose a beagle over his orders.
c6_jail.recap.01.speaker: steve

c6_jail.recap.03.text: Stephen and Iris were waiting behind Gus’s bakery next door, where nobody would see our faces.
c6_jail.recap.03.speaker: steve

c7_gate.talk.stephen.2.02.text: He knows you’re not me, Stephen. He just likes you better.
c7_gate.talk.stephen.2.02.speaker: steve

i2_nora.in.04.text: The glass stayed shut while three blue strips counted our breaths. The beds did the work until each of us could breathe alone.
i2_nora.in.04.speaker: nora

i2_nora.in.05.text: Only then did the latches release. WAKE COMPLETE, the panel said. MIRROR LINK ACTIVE.
i2_nora.in.05.speaker: nora

c10_station.relay.lead.01.text: The club sent signal three yesterday, without me. Today I’m sending signal four. Let’s see who keeps up.
c10_station.relay.lead.01.speaker: frank

c2_ship.escape.03.text: Prefect? I did not ask for a release. The scan is not finished.
c2_ship.escape.03.speaker: guard

c2_ship.escape.04.text: Prefect, please repeat your instruction. The chair says you released it.
c2_ship.escape.04.speaker: guard

c2_ship.escape.05.text: The attendant is busy arguing with the column. Quietly, now.
c2_ship.escape.05.speaker: steve

c2_ship.intake.02.text: Something is in the water! Something big!
c2_ship.intake.02.speaker: guard

c2_ship.intake.lead.01.text: I gave no release. Look at the chair.
c2_ship.intake.lead.01.speaker: saren

c2_ship.intake.lead.02.text: The chair is empty! Prefect, the human is gone!
c2_ship.intake.lead.02.speaker: guard

c2_ship.intake.lead.03.text: The brass hatch in the floor. That’s the intake valve. Flood the tunnel, and they’ll have to swim after me.
c2_ship.intake.lead.03.speaker: steve

c2_ship.intake.lead.04.text: Water in the intake! The human is in the tunnel!
c2_ship.intake.lead.04.speaker: guard

c2_ship.intake.lead.05.text: Admiral swims the whole bay at night. If he hears the right whistle, he’ll come.
c2_ship.intake.lead.05.speaker: steve

c2_ship.intake.lead.06.text: Please stop! You are not finished!
c2_ship.intake.lead.06.speaker: guard

c2_ship.intake.lead.07.text: Nora’s spool, the loose copy, or the Prefect. One chance.
c2_ship.intake.lead.07.speaker: steve

c2_ship.recap.03.text: And the woman with Nora’s face, who locked me out on the balcony and then let me go, had walked me to that chair herself.
c2_ship.recap.03.speaker: steve

c4_escape.out.02.text: Kidnapping Nora. And they’ll scan June tonight, because she stayed behind for me. I can’t get back up that hill alone. I have to keep moving.
c4_escape.out.02.speaker: steve

c4_safe.in.07.text: He took every tape I’d brought, even Mom’s voicemail. An hour later he handed that one back. Not evidence, he said.
c4_safe.in.07.speaker: steve

c4_safe.match.02.text: Not here, Mercer. Not with Adrian’s agents in the hall.
c4_safe.match.02.speaker: calder

c7_gate.talk.stephen.3.02.text: I only told him the truth. You were very close. You were right under the sound desk.
c7_gate.talk.stephen.3.02.speaker: stephen

c7_gate.truck.lead.01.text: Inside the fence, I climbed out from under the sound desk, tripped over a cable and landed at the feet of the woman running the sound check.
c7_gate.truck.lead.01.speaker: steve

c7_swap.bus.lead.04.text: The press van feeds the national broadcast. Keep the tone off it, or every copy watching at home hears it too.
c7_swap.bus.lead.04.speaker: stephen

c7_swap.recap.02.text: Iris told me later that the tone pulled at her too. She held on to June’s sleeve and counted Sunday dinners until it passed. Beside me, Stephen gripped the desk with both hands and did not turn.
c7_swap.recap.02.speaker: steve

c8_rig.path.lead.04.text: My crew pass still opens the antenna passage. I checked. Twice. Cancelling it would put Saren’s mistake on the record.
c8_rig.path.lead.04.speaker: stephen

c9_choir.in.06.text: The straps opened. The crew let go of Stephen. Even Saren stepped back from the console.
c9_choir.in.06.speaker: steve

c9_choir.in.07.text: We followed you down from row nine. Nobody stopped us. The whole crew had stopped to listen.
c9_choir.in.07.speaker: calder

epilogue.talk.rook_copy.1.01.text: I’m leaving town today. I want to find out who I am when nobody is watching.
epilogue.talk.rook_copy.1.01.speaker: rook_copy

c8_beach.second.03.text: Rook kept this tape for an hour at the safe house. Long enough to copy it.
c8_beach.second.03.speaker: steve

c10_live.in.02.text: Steve. I know you. Dad’s name is... Frank. It’s on my hand.
c10_live.in.02.speaker: stephen

c10_live.second.find.text: Reed brought the coast into the booth. Wen took the handoff. Both grids answered.
c10_live.second.find.speaker: steve

c10_live.second.lead.05.text: I’m standing by. Wait for my green lamp.
c10_live.second.lead.05.speaker: wen

c10_live.third.find.text: The tape stopped. Three hundred and twelve voices came through the open channel.
c10_live.third.find.speaker: steve

c10_live.third.lead.02.text: I’ll run the reel. Leave the tail on that last gust.
c10_live.third.lead.02.speaker: steve

c10_live.third.lead.03.text: Watch my lamp. When it goes dark, the channel is theirs.
c10_live.third.lead.03.speaker: wen

c10_report.in.06.text: I can still hear my mother in that ship. If you reconcile me, will I know her voice?
c10_report.in.06.speaker: saren

c10_station.ctx.03.text: Five weeks after Halcyon fired me, I sat at my old desk and stopped waiting for somebody else to take the microphone.
c10_station.ctx.03.speaker: steve

c10_station.relay.find.text: The official line sent back yesterday’s test signal. Cedar can repeat a test number but can’t see the field. Marsh, out past Sentinel Point, answered with a fresh wind reading. Marsh is our eyes, and Gull carries the live-show cues down the coast.
c10_station.relay.find.speaker: steve

c10_station.relay.lead.02.text: The official channel just sent back three. That’s yesterday’s test signal.
c10_station.relay.lead.02.speaker: steve

c10_town.in.05.text: Wind through the western towers. Last evening. Shore dub from the original take.
c10_town.in.05.speaker: agnes

c10_town.in.09.text: On ninth nights I answered whatever shore phone rang. A few bars on the line kept my borrowed memories aligned. At the boathouse, you watched me do it.
c10_town.in.09.speaker: agnes

c10_town.lights.lead.01.text: Two street captains, one spare phone and two streets of porch lights. Easy.
c10_town.lights.lead.01.speaker: nora

c10_town.out.03.text: I made this dub before I came ashore, Steven. Before I had hands that smelled of herring.
c10_town.out.03.speaker: agnes

c10_town.recap.02.text: The porch lights on Pier and Orchard are waiting for my cue. Shaw has the lamps, Wen has the grid, and the Choir will answer live.
c10_town.recap.02.speaker: steve

c1_dinner.ctx.03.text: A ring had been in my sock drawer for a year. I kept telling myself I would ask Nora after one of these dinners.
c1_dinner.ctx.03.speaker: steve

c1_dinner.ctx.04.text: Nora’s oldest dinner rule was that nobody touched her plate. That night Carmen moved it twice, and Nora only smiled.
c1_dinner.ctx.04.speaker: steve

c1_escape.order.01.text: At 20:15 Nora was in Carmen’s photo, across the bay. Her staff credential was used in the north wing at that same minute.
c1_escape.order.01.speaker: steve

c1_escape.order.find.text: Someone used Nora’s name and staff credential in the north wing while she was at her mother’s birthday, across the bay. And now Nora has locked me out on the balcony.
c1_escape.order.find.speaker: steve

c1_escape.order.lead.02.text: N. Reyes, Nora’s staff number, 20:30. She always said that north-wing clock runs fifteen minutes fast.
c1_escape.order.lead.02.speaker: steve

c1_escape.recap.01.text: My list: one good morning, played twice. A whistle Admiral won’t answer. Nora’s credential used across the bay. A phone call about a notebook. A locked door.
c1_escape.recap.01.speaker: steve

c1_flat.in.09.text: I kept the spare cassettes in my sock drawer. The little velvet box was still there. I took two tapes and shut the drawer.
c1_flat.in.09.speaker: steve

c2_aquarium.out.05.text: The old intake is open. I have the service key. This way.
c2_aquarium.out.05.speaker: lyle_copy

c2_aquarium.recap.02.text: Nora was here, whistling for help. I didn’t hear her for five months.
c2_aquarium.recap.02.speaker: steve

c2_ship.command.lead.06.text: The tape keeps moving after the click. Blank tape, not leader. There’s room left.
c2_ship.command.lead.06.speaker: steve

c2_ship.command.lead.07.text: Thank you, escorts. It is nearly dawn, and the town will expect you at breakfast.
c2_ship.command.lead.07.speaker: guard

c2_ship.escape.02.text: It worked. Index sixty-one percent, and all of me is getting out of this chair.
c2_ship.escape.02.speaker: steve

c2_ship.escape.find.text: The Prefect’s own voice opened the chair at the notch marked sixty-one. The memory index stopped at sixty-one percent; whatever it could bind would come later.
c2_ship.escape.find.speaker: steve

c2_ship.in.04.text: Lyle unlocked the old intake and walked me down the tunnel under the bay. At the end of it there was a ship.
c2_ship.in.04.speaker: steve

c2_ship.recap.02.text: They tried to make another me. The memory index stopped at sixty-one percent. I didn’t know yet what the tank would bind from it.
c2_ship.recap.02.speaker: steve

c3_archive.out.11.text: At four minutes past midnight, the boathouse phone rang once. Mrs. Penhallow answered, listened without speaking, and hung up.
c3_archive.out.11.speaker: steve

c3_archive.out.12.text: I’m calling Adrian Rook. FBI. He owes me a favor from a kidnapping case twenty years ago.
c3_archive.out.12.speaker: calder

c3_archive.out.13.text: An hour later my flip phone buzzed. A text, from a number I didn’t know.
c3_archive.out.13.speaker: steve

c3_house.crossword.lead.01.text: You told me that chair indexes the oldest memories first. And you stopped it at sixty-one percent.
c3_house.crossword.lead.01.speaker: calder

c3_house.mail.find.text: Dale had my letters bundled for June’s house at 08:04. The post office didn’t know until 08:12. The private channel log says only Lyle took June’s call at ten past six. He told Dale.
c3_house.mail.find.speaker: steve

c3_house.rules.lead.04.text: Walt moved to Washington in April. The clerk’s bound ledger puts him at her counter on May third while a sworn hearing transcript has him testifying in Washington.
c3_house.rules.lead.04.speaker: calder

c4_safe.ctx.01.text: Adrian Rook arrived two afternoons later with four agents and two black SUVs. He was everything June had promised. Calm. Kind. Thorough.
c4_safe.ctx.01.speaker: steve

c5_shack.in.06.text: I heard stories about the bay singing when I was a boy. I first heard it myself three years ago. Your father was the only one who asked what it sounded like.
c5_shack.in.06.speaker: luis

c5_station.in.01.text: Breaking news, folks: there’s a fella in our control room!
c5_station.in.01.speaker: autorick

c5_station.out.06.text: In a glass tank, last Friday. Cold, wet, with the index at sixty-one. A very tall man gave me a crew pass, an earpiece and a job.
c5_station.out.06.speaker: stephen

c5_station.recap.02.text: And the man with my face had a sixty-one-percent memory index, but his last stable binding ended at breakfast before the boat. Eighteen months of my life were missing.
c5_station.recap.02.speaker: steve

c5_station.stephen.03.text: The tank slate said sixty-one was the memory index, not sixty-one percent of a person. Last stable binding: breakfast in Dad’s shack.
c5_station.stephen.03.speaker: stephen

c5_station.stephen.04.text: Call me Stephen. One of us should sound like a grown-up.
c5_station.stephen.04.speaker: stephen

c6_iris.recap.01.text: I came to the pier expecting a trap. Instead she gave me a test I could repeat and a warning I could check.
c6_iris.recap.01.speaker: steve

c6_iris.takes.lead.02.text: The first re-sync window passed while I was chasing you. I still escorted you below later, but the window had closed. The second time, I chose not to go.
c6_iris.takes.lead.02.speaker: iris

c7_gate.out.06.text: In the fog between the antennas, an old woman was carrying a bait bucket. Mrs. Penhallow. Miles from her pier, again.
c7_gate.out.06.speaker: steve

c8_beach.second.find.text: Saren’s message is Mom’s voicemail, cut and stitched: the same breath before ‘kiddo’, and a gap where ‘The bay is singing’ used to be. He has no message from her. He has the personal copy Rook made while he held my cassette.
c8_beach.second.find.speaker: steve

c8_lab.notebook.find.text: America staged its test first, and China built its own from a copy, missing beat and all. Both announced themselves with the same public handshake and went out over open radio, so something out there recorded them. Mom heard that missing beat again in the bay. The fleet came because of a show.
c8_lab.notebook.find.speaker: steve

c8_lab.notebook.lead.04.text: Both teams began with the same open-radio handshake. It told every listener when the performance started.
c8_lab.notebook.lead.04.speaker: wen

c8_lab.notebook.lead.05.text: Both tests went out over open radio. Anyone with a receiver could hear them.
c8_lab.notebook.lead.05.speaker: wen

c8_lab.notebook.lead.06.text: And the minutes of the meeting at one table quote both tests. Your mother was in that room.
c8_lab.notebook.lead.06.speaker: wen

c8_lab.talk.wen.2.01.text: I walked here from the hotel. An old woman carrying a bait bucket said good morning to me in Mandarin.
c8_lab.talk.wen.2.01.speaker: wen

c9_choir.in.05.text: The chair dragged every memory past me, but it wasn’t erasing them. Across the rail, Stephen stared at his hand. Frank. Dad. His link was failing, not mine.
c9_choir.in.05.speaker: steve

c9_gallery.recap.01.text: Nora was on her feet. Iris was still herself. For the moment, that was enough.
c9_gallery.recap.01.speaker: steve

c9_gallery.recap.02.text: Stephen took the rig toward the antenna. Then Nora led me to row nine.
c9_gallery.recap.02.speaker: steve

c9_wake.ctx.02.text: Iris stayed with the newly awake near Nora’s bed. Pell and Biscuit held the service hatch behind us.
c9_wake.ctx.02.speaker: steve

c9_wake.frank.find.text: Dad answered the Thursday net before he even opened his eyes.
c9_wake.frank.find.speaker: steve

c9_wake.frank.lead.03.text: Give me the speaker. I can hold it against his ear.
c9_wake.frank.lead.03.speaker: nora

c9_wake.frank.lead.04.text: Listen for the Morse. The Thursday club calling him in.
c9_wake.frank.lead.04.speaker: steve

c9_wake.helen.find.text: The tape ran out. Mom held the last note a little longer.
c9_wake.helen.find.speaker: steve

c9_wake.helen.lead.03.text: Up two steps. Down past home. Then back up, and hold that last note.
c9_wake.helen.lead.03.speaker: frank

c9_wake.recap.01.text: Dad was shivering. I put his old cardigan around him. He found the hole in the cuff with his thumb, the way he always did.
c9_wake.recap.01.speaker: steve

epilogue.bait.find.text: Two Mrs. Penhallows, one counter, and people are finally buying bait. The Long Patience was already gone. One Adrian Rook stayed; the other took the morning ferry to find out who he was.
epilogue.bait.find.speaker: steve

i2_nora.ctx.02.text: The bed panel said Monday, November fifth. That was how I learned five months had passed.
i2_nora.ctx.02.speaker: nora

i2_nora.ctx.03.text: I was frightened for about a minute. Then I did what I do at any party where nobody knows each other. I started learning names.
i2_nora.ctx.03.speaker: nora

c10_live.recap.01.text: The wind was a dub. The porch lights, field lamps, two grids, radios and three hundred and twelve human voices all answered it live.
c10_live.recap.01.speaker: steve

c10_live.second.lead.04.text: Coast next. Bring me a live reply before we switch on the grid.
c10_live.second.lead.04.speaker: steve

c10_report.in.05.text: They first bound you in a cradle ship after our star went dark. Fear was your first record.
c10_report.in.05.speaker: archivist

c10_town.in.10.text: That city was our home. Our star went dark. This is the last wind that ever blew through those streets.
c10_town.in.10.speaker: agnes

c10_town.recap.01.text: The last sound of a whole city fit in the bottom of her bait bucket.
c10_town.recap.01.speaker: steve

c10_town.wind.find.text: The pencil mark comes just after the last gust. That’s where I open the return. The wind is on tape. The people answering it are here.
c10_town.wind.find.speaker: steve

c3_house.mail.lead.03.text: Monday morning, I used the private car-to-station handset. Only my deputy was on that channel. I heard him answer.
c3_house.mail.lead.03.speaker: calder

c3_house.rules.find.text: Two names held up. The deputy and the permit signer each turned up in two places at once. Going to your boys’ games proves nothing.
c3_house.rules.find.speaker: steve

c3_house.rules.lead.03.text: Lyle signed a parking citation here in town. The same minute, a nurse took his blood pressure at a clinic two counties away. I spoke to her.
c3_house.rules.lead.03.speaker: calder

c8_beach.ctx.01.text: The Prefect met me alone at dawn. He set a little Newton’s cradle on a flat rock and let one ball drop. He watched it instead of looking at me.
c8_beach.ctx.01.speaker: steve

c2_ship.in.07.text: The memory index opens with the oldest records. Binding runs separately. Here is your driving test. Congratulations. You passed.
c2_ship.in.07.speaker: guard

i2_nora.recap.02.text: I counted thirteen months of silence before they took me. Five more went by while I slept. I still want to hear what he has to say.
i2_nora.recap.02.speaker: nora

c1_flat.saturday.find.text: Saturday. Red tape. First the station, then Nora in the doorway. You can hear me answer her.
c1_flat.saturday.find.speaker: steve

c4_escape.van.02.text: I unclipped the spare radio from the bulkhead, eased the rear door on the blind turn, and dropped into the ferns in the rain. Neither of them saw a thing. The taillights kept right on down the hill.
c4_escape.van.02.speaker: steve

c4_escape.van.find.text: On the gravel bend, with both agents watching the road ahead and the catch off, I slipped out the rear door unseen with the spare radio and rolled into the soft ditch.
c4_escape.van.find.speaker: steve

c4_escape.van.lead.01.text: Both agents up front behind the mesh. No cuffs, just a witness in the back, and a rear catch that comes off for gravel.
c4_escape.van.lead.01.speaker: steve

c6_iris.alibi.find.text: At 8:10 by the radio, Stephen stood beside his own wanted poster at Gus’s bread window while Gus fixed the smudge. The crowd and the cops ran up the lane to the bakery, leaving the pier quiet for my meeting.
c6_iris.alibi.find.speaker: steve

c6_iris.ctx.02.text: On Monday morning my flip phone buzzed, so we slipped down to the waterfront corner between Gus’s bakery and the pier.
c6_iris.ctx.02.speaker: steve

c6_iris.hold.lead.02.text: At four minutes past midnight on the thirtieth, I phoned two Halcyon offices from these payphones and taped both calls.
c6_iris.hold.lead.02.speaker: iris

i2_nora.jobs.01.text: I’ll trip the wash chute and hold the pods while you cross.
i2_nora.jobs.01.speaker: lyle

i2_nora.jobs.find.text: Lyle trips the north wash chute to draw the guard off. Dale keeps lookout and maps the rows. I take the pumps. Water is the one thing on this ship I understand.
i2_nora.jobs.find.speaker: nora

i2_nora.jobs.lead.02.text: That north wash chute by the arch jams if you trip the return latch. I can pull it when you say go.
i2_nora.jobs.lead.02.speaker: lyle

i2_nora.jobs.lead.03.text: Thirty years on a mail route. Put me on lookout and I’ll log every row and pod number in this place.
i2_nora.jobs.lead.03.speaker: dale

i2_nora.message.find.text: My message for Steve is queued in Slot B on Bed Three’s terminal. It will wait for him.
i2_nora.message.find.speaker: nora

i2_nora.patrol.find.text: The jammed wash chute pulled the guard into the north shaft and locked the bulkhead behind him for six minutes. Lyle and Dale are watching the pods, and the Gallery aisle is clear.
i2_nora.patrol.find.speaker: nora

i2_nora.patrol.lead.01.text: He never leaves the aisle for a shift bell, and a pod warning brings him straight to us.
i2_nora.patrol.lead.01.speaker: nora

i2_nora.patrol.lead.02.text: Only a north wash-chute jam pulls him through that archway, and the bulkhead locks behind him for a six-minute wash clear.
i2_nora.patrol.lead.02.speaker: nora

i2_nora.patrol.01.text: There goes the chute alarm. He’s through the archway, and the bulkhead locked behind him. The aisle is ours.
i2_nora.patrol.01.speaker: nora

book.after.4.3.text: Nora argues with me again. About everything. I missed it more than I can say.
book.after.4.3.speaker: steve

book.aftermath.2.2.text: Mom called me from the boat that night. I dubbed her phone voicemail onto a cassette. Most nights I play it at three in the morning. I don’t know what I’m listening for.
book.aftermath.2.2.speaker: steve
